title: Close cfml binding gaps found in cfml-m1.2 review
description:
## Outcome
calc_fml::bind_references gives a typed site, or a typed refusal, for every reference form the cfml-m1.2 review found unhandled, and the cfml_m1_2 cases fail under the mutants that survived that review.

## Context
Found by cfml-m1.2's round-3 review (2026-10-20). Each item is a binding defect in crates/calc-fml/src/reference/bind.rs or a case that does not exercise a rule. None of them stops cfml-m1.3: the evaluator binds through the same binder, so a fix here reaches it. CalcFml files only.

## Do
- `={A1}`: a reference inside an array constant is not a live operand (Binder::walk has no ArrayLiteralExpr arm, bind.rs:128-131). Give it a typed refusal; Excel refuses the entry.
- `=Sheet2!#REF!` is refused as QualifiedNonReference; give it the #REF! value route instead.
- `=#REF!(A1)` parses as an invoke and binds A1 on the anchor's sheet; refuse or bind it as Excel reads it. Restore that exact input to the acceptance case (it was changed to `=#REF!SUM(A1)`).
- `=$B`, `=$3`, `=$XFE`, `=Sheet2!$B`, `=Sheet2!$3` give no site and no diagnostic (bind.rs:156, 181-186); a `$` form cannot be a name, so each gets a typed refusal, and the unit test at bind.rs:444 changes with it.
- Two-sheet ranges: `=Sheet2!A1:Sheet1!B2` asks the catalogue four times; `=Nope!B3:Sheet2!D7` never binds or reports the Sheet2 end. Assert the request counts and the sites.
- Surviving mutants: `lone-outside-grid-always-refused` (bind.rs:181; assert `=A1+0`, `=IF(A1>0,1,2)` and `=A1*1048577` each give only the A1 site), `deleted-pair-not-one-sheet` and `external-span-left-not-one-sheet` (bind.rs:209; assert `=#REF!A1:#REF!B2` and `=[B.xlsx]S!A1:[B.xlsx]S!B2`). Each mutant must turn a cfml_m1_2 case red.
- read_cells with a multi-cell CellRun::Values run that wraps a row boundary (read.rs:139-153): a reader that returns such runs, and assertions on the cells and positions.
- Migration record cfml-m1.2.json: move AxisRef and ReferenceNotation to a written-fresh entry (coords.rs lookup exits 1), and drop the fields AGENTS.md does not list.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p calc-fml --test acceptance cfml_m1_2 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id cfml-m1.2 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cfml-m1.2 --platform wasm --require-all
```
Each mutant above, applied by hand, fails the first command; keep the diff and the failing output under target/accept/cfml-m1.2/.

## Out of scope
Excel measurement of these readings (the owner's capture bead). Name and LAMBDA binding (cfml-m3.1).
notes:
Claimed 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the main clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc while cfml-m1.3 is built in DnaCalc-cfml (it adds crates/calc-fml/src/eval/ and cfml_m1_3 cases; this bead stays in reference/ and the cfml_m1_2 cases, so the two merge).
- The capability: every reference form the cfml-m1.2 review found unhandled gets a typed site or a typed refusal, so cfml-m1.3's evaluator never receives a silently dropped or wrongly bound reference.
- Rulings: `={A1}` is a typed refusal (Excel refuses a reference inside an array constant at entry). `=Sheet2!#REF!` binds to a deleted-reference operand whose placement gives #REF!, as `#REF!A1` does. `=#REF!(A1)`: a typed refusal unless the parser reads it as Excel does; restore that exact input to the case. `$`-only forms (`=$B`, `=$3`, `=$XFE`, `=Sheet2!$B`, `=Sheet2!$3`) are typed refusals, never silent.
- Done when the Do list holds and each named mutant fails a cfml_m1_2 case.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-10-20. calc_fml::bind_references gives a typed site or a typed refusal for every form cfml-m1.2's round-3 review listed: ={A1} is refused (InArrayConstant); =Sheet2!#REF! binds as ReferenceShape::Deleted and places as PlacementError::DeletedCells (#REF!); =#REF!(A1) is refused whole; =$B, =$3, =Sheet2!$B and =Sheet2!$3 are refused (LoneRowOrColumn), =$XFE as OutsideGrid; two-sheet ranges look each sheet up once and report each end. read_cells is tested with runs that continue past a row's end. AxisRef and ReferenceNotation are written-fresh entries in the record.
Evidence: commit eb669eb. cfml-m1.2 windows, wasm (Chrome and Firefox) and linux --require-all passed 2 of 2 (linux in WSL at eb669eb); cfml-m1.1 windows, wasm and linux passed 2 of 2. The three named mutants and six probes undoing this bead's fixes each fail a cfml_m1_2 case; two refuters and a judge (who closed it) found no missing Do item and no honesty-rule breach.
Still open: the remaining binder inconsistencies the judge listed are dc-t2gu; Excel's readings of these forms are dc-ds2z; no product caller of bind_references until cfml-m1.3 lands.

title: Resolve INDIRECT's A1 text to a reference through calc_fml, ahead of OFFSET and the reference operators
description:
## Outcome
INDIRECT(ref_text) with A1-style text (a cell, a range, a sheet-qualified range, quoted sheet names, absolute and relative forms) resolves through calc_fml's binder to the reference Excel resolves, so a formula such as INDEX(INDIRECT(sheet&"!$A$9:$BF$96"),...) computes through calc_fml::evaluate, and the evaluation reports the cells it read as a dynamic read footprint the engine can use; text Excel cannot resolve gives #REF!, as Excel does.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison (dc-3t1b, 2026-10-21): INDIRECT is the function-missing root of 252 cells in Default-tariff-cap-level, all of one shape, INDEX(INDIRECT(cell&"..."),MATCH(...,INDIRECT(...)),MATCH(...,INDIRECT(...))); calc_fml's compile refuses the name. INDIRECT sits in cfml-m3.3 with OFFSET and the reference operators (union, intersection, spill, @), whose scope is wider; this bead takes INDIRECT out of cfml-m3.3 so it lands now. Making the engine re-dirty and reschedule on the reads INDIRECT reports is ceng-m3.3's (dynamic read overlays), which follows. Library: CalcFml.

## Do
- INDIRECT as a catalogued call whose result is a reference resolved from text by calc_fml's binder in the formula's workbook context (sheet names, quoted names, $ forms, ranges, a whole column or row); a1=FALSE (R1C1 text) measured and implemented, or refused as not modelled naming cfml-m3.3; a defined name in the text refused as not modelled naming cfml-m3.3 unless the binder resolves names already.
- The evaluation reports the area INDIRECT resolved as a read footprint (the ReadObserver route), and INDIRECT is marked volatile if the catalogue has that property.
- Rows labelled documented or measured, an oracle workbook from the committed generator, `cargo xtask capture`, and a comparison case through calc_verdict, including INDIRECT nested in INDEX and MATCH as the Ofgem shape uses it, an unresolvable text (#REF!), and a reference to another sheet.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
Every row calc_fml computes matches the capture; rows another bead owns are published as not modelled under it.

## Out of scope
OFFSET and the reference operators (cfml-m3.3); the engine's dynamic dependency edges (ceng-m3.3).

title: Judge a capture whose shared-formula ref spans cells outside its group, as Excel saves them
description:
## Outcome
A CaptureRecord of an Excel-saved workbook is judged, not refused, when a shared-formula ref covers cells of other groups, normal formulas, constants or empty cells, so `cargo xtask capture` writes a record of real workbooks instead of exiting 5.

## Context
Measured 2026-10-21 on the three Ofgem price-cap workbooks downloaded with the owner's yes (C:\Work\DnaCalc\corpus\ofgem-price-cap-2026q4): 27 of 119 shared groups (Annex-4), 11 of 488 (Annex-9) and 103 of 2,581 (Default-tariff-cap-level) have refs whose cells include other shared groups, normal formulas, constants or styled empty cells; no group has a member outside its ref. calc-verdict's check_shared_ranges (tools/calc-verdict/src/verdict.rs) refuses any range cell that is not a group member, and `cargo xtask capture` runs that check through its file-cache replay, so no record of these files can be written. calc-doc already tolerates the holes (crates/calc-doc/src/load/sheet.rs).

## Do
- Keep: the range is on a listed sheet; one range per group; every group cell lies inside its range; every group has a range.
- Remove: every cell of the range must be a group cell. Say in the doc comment that completeness of the denominator rests on the worker's cross-check against Excel's own SpecialCells(xlCellTypeFormulas), whose failures already refuse the record.
- Update the unit test that pins the old message; note on infra-m1.3 that the rule was checked against real captures and changed here.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
```
A record whose shared ref C1:C8 lists 6 group cells, with a normal formula at C4 and no formula at C7, is judged with all 7 formula cells in the denominator; a group member outside its ref is still refused.

## Out of scope
Capturing the Ofgem workbooks (the Ofgem comparison bead).
close_reason: Built in 60c338d (calc-verdict): a version 2 capture whose shared-formula ref covers cells outside its group (other groups, ordinary formulas, constants, empty cells) is judged, through judge and through the file-cache replay `cargo xtask capture` runs, with every listed formula cell in the denominator once; a group member outside its ref is still refused with the cell named. Measured: the three Ofgem packages (Excel for the web) hold such refs in 27/119, 11/488 and 103/2,581 groups; desktop Excel 16.0.20430 saves a fill of B1:B500 with the last ref B449:B512. Case dc_61sj__shared_ref_with_holes_judged passed on windows and wasm (Chrome and Firefox) at cd89d6d plus the change, and on linux in WSL at 60c338d; infra-m1.1 passed on windows and linux; dc-qguw passed on windows; infra-m0.1 passed on windows at 60c338d (one earlier run failed on cargo last-use tracker .global-cache, filed as dc-pw05). One round; the judge allowed the close; the orchestrator applied the follow-ups and a read-only reviewer checked them. Its calculated counts rest on version 1 evaluation fixtures (dc-i1ro). Non-live records: dc-dhlu. Real Ofgem captures: dc-3t1b.

title: CalcVBA: a VBA object is one COM object, investigate removing wrapper mapping
description:
Question (owner, 2026-11-20): a VBA class instance is itself a COM object. It implements IUnknown, and
its one identity also answers IDispatch, its default dual interface (_ClassName), every Implements
interface, and IConnectionPointContainer / ISupportErrorInfo where they apply. Why does CalcVBA map project
objects to separate wrapper objects instead?

What the code does today (CalcVBA master, 2026-11-20):
- calcvba-runtime object_ref.rs CompatObjectBase: the runtime project object has a three-slot IUnknown
  vtable. compat_query_interface answers IID_IUnknown only (dc-yqq0.15), because answering IDispatch or a
  class interface with that vtable would let foreign code call slots that are not there.
- calcvba-com windows_runtime_object.rs RuntimeObjectDispatch (via automation::project_dispatch): the
  IDispatch a project object gets when it crosses to foreign code from VM3/JIT/Declare. It is a separate
  wrapper with its own refcount; GetIDsOfNames answers DISP_E_UNKNOWNNAME and Invoke DISP_E_MEMBERNOTFOUND.
- calcvba-comhost lib.rs DispatchObject: the in-process COM server's wrapper (IDispatch, bounded dual
  vtables, imported-interface faces, ISupportErrorInfo, connection points) around an ObjectRef. A WRAPPERS
  map keyed by the object's identity makes one wrapper per live object (commit 45a3a0c1), so Is holds.
- calcvba-native-template server.rs Object: the COM EXE server's object is a compiled vtable plus a
  type library served through DispInvoke, around the compiled instance pointer.

Investigate:
- Can the runtime object itself carry the real interface set (IDispatch, the dual class interface from the
  compiled vtable/type info, Implements interfaces, connection points), so one COM identity serves VBA and
  foreign callers and no wrapper or wrapper map is needed?
- What each executor (VM3, JIT, AOT/native template) needs for that: a vtable per class, a member entry per
  slot, and DispInvoke over a type library, as the EXE server already does.
- Lifetime and identity rules: QueryInterface for IUnknown returns the same pointer, refcounts are shared,
  Class_Terminate runs once on the owning thread, and foreign threads post the final release.
- What can be removed afterwards: RuntimeObjectDispatch, comhost DispatchObject/WRAPPERS, and the
  bridge's runtime_object_from_dispatch unwrapping.

Done: a design note with the recommended object layout and a list of follow-up beads, or a recorded reason
to keep wrappers. Lower priority than the VARIANT migration (epic dc-yqq0).

CompatObjectBase carries ClassDualVtbl + MemberInvoker; RuntimeObjectDispatch, the bridge wrapper cache and the comhost WRAPPERS map are gone (no occurrence in CalcVBA 80f29300f). Verified live on Win64 by vw1/ww1.

title: CalcVBA: Let takes the default member of an object held in a Variant or Object value (run time)
description:
VBA's Let takes the default member of an object that a Variant or Object value holds at run time. CalcVBA does that only when the source's static type is a class or interface with a known default member, at bind time. When the static type is Variant or Object, VM3 and the JIT store the object itself.

Evidence (2026-11-15):
- Excel probe temp/variant-layout-probe/tw11 through the VBA loader: `v = ws.[A1]` and `v = Sheet1.[A1]` (v As Variant; the result of Worksheet's DISPID_EVALUATE member is a Variant holding a Range) give Double 42 in VBA; CalcVBA VM3 and JIT store the Range ("obj Range").
- No Excel needed: project class Dflt with a default `Property Get Value` = 42. `Set w = New Dflt: v = w` (w As Variant), `v = Make()` (a Variant function returning the object), and `Set o = New Dflt: v = o` (o As Object) all leave v holding the object on both backends (calcvba-cli run-project). `v = d` with d As Dflt gives Integer 42 (the bind-time path).

Work: a run-time Let coercion for a Let whose target is not an object and whose source is statically Variant or Object. If the value holds an object, call its default member (project class default, or DISPID_VALUE through IDispatch), repeating while the result is again an object. Raise VBA's error when there is none: measure which (438, or 91 for Nothing) on a small Excel probe first, together with ByVal arguments, which VBA does not default (global10 passed `ActiveSheet.[B2]` to a function and got the Range). Implement it once for VM3 and the JIT (an OxIR instruction or a shared rt-abi helper). Then add the tw11 lines and the Dflt cases as tests.
close_reason: CalcVBA 99ed9de06: CoreValue::LetValue (IsObject + late default get, VM3 and JIT; typed host default_value_of). Excel let12: all Let cases match VBA (incl. 438/450/91, chain one level, Range, late call); tw11 ws.[A1] / Sheet1.[A1] give 42. Conversions/operators remain dc-pfk4c.

title: Match Excel's bits on the six cells where the Ofgem comparison found a 1-ulp arithmetic difference
description:
## Outcome
calc_func's arithmetic gives Excel's binary64 result on the three formula shapes where the Ofgem comparison found DNA Calc 1 ulp away from Excel, or each is recorded as a measured bit variant with the operation that differs named.

## Context
The first `cargo xtask compare` of Ofgem Annex-4 and Annex-9 against this machine's Excel (dc-3t1b, 2026-10-21) found 3 kernel-bits cells out of 40,450 calculated; every other calculated cell matched. Each agrees with Excel to 15 significant digits and differs by 1 ulp, and in each the reads equal Excel's values (constants, or formula cells that matched):
- two Annex-4 cells of the shape IF(x="-","-",SUM(seven cells)*k+y) (DNA gives the correctly rounded IEEE result of a left-to-right SUM; Excel is 1 ulp away, one up and one down);
- one Annex-9 cell of the shape IFERROR(IF(a>0,a*(c/(b+c)),"0"),"-") (DNA gives the correctly rounded result of a*(c/(b+c)), which is also the exactly rounded value of the whole expression; Excel gives 1 ulp more).
Tested offline and ruled out: IEEE double with left-to-right evaluation, x87 80-bit intermediates for the sum and the product, division as multiplication by a reciprocal, and a*c/(b+c). The triage key (IF, IFERROR) is inferred; the difference lies in the arithmetic. The cell values are in the local compare output (C:\Work\DnaCalc\corpus\compare, outside the repository, licence unverified): commit no Ofgem values or text.
A function bit variant: recorded apart, it holds up no document, formula, engine or host work.

## Do
- In Excel on this machine, split each shape into its sub-expressions in separate cells (with the local Ofgem values, read-only, nothing committed) and find which operation's bits differ from IEEE double.
- Build synthetic reproducers of the same shape (searched values, not Ofgem's) as oracle rows from the committed generator, capture them, and find the rule (for example a summation order or precision in SUM, or an operation Excel does not round to nearest).
- Implement the rule if it is general and measured; otherwise record the rows as measured bit variants under this bead with a typed result kept and the difference counted.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
```
The synthetic rows match Excel's capture bit for bit, or each is published with its measured difference under this bead; a re-run of the Ofgem compare shows the three cells matched or still counted here.

## Out of scope
Other functions' bit differences (each its own bead).
close_reason: All 11 Ofgem cells that differed are fixed (db6dbf7): Excel does + - * / (and SUM, PRODUCT, AVERAGE, SUMSQ) in the x87 unit at 64-bit precision and then stores to binary64, so near-ties double-round to the other neighbour; the engine now does the same on x86_64, and off x86 (wasm) a portable emulation matches the hardware on 400,000 random pairs per operation. Evidence: Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272 (was 209,261); oracle rows for this rule 108 failing before, 0 after; cargo xtask check passed at a55c79c. Still open: other kernel bits under dc-j9k; the x87 function route in the browser under dc-8dg.

Six cells in all across the three workbooks, all of them SUM(...)*k or a*(c/(b+c)) shapes; the measurement this bead does covers them.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text: Function exactness lane, 2026-10-23 (commit db6dbf7): root cause found and fixed. Excel computes + - * / (operators and the SUM/PRODUCT/AVERAGE/SUMSQ folds) on the x87 unit at 64-bit precision and stores to binary64: double rounding RN53(RN64(x)). Each of the 11 Ofgem cells had an exact product, quotient or sum within 1/4096 ulp of a midpoint (e.g. Annex-4 products 0.4999 ulp from their rounding), so the double rounding goes to the even neighbour. calc-func Site arithmetic now uses excel_numeric::excel_x87_add/sub/mul/div; off x86_64 a portable emulation (excel_numeric::pc64) tested equal to the hardware. title: Store authored cells in calc-doc-model as immutable shared sparse pages
description:
## Outcome
calc-doc-model's ModelRoot holds each sheet's authored cell inputs (CellInput: values and formula text) in immutable, Arc-shared sparse pages. Reads are borrowed: one cell, and the occupied cells of a sheet or rectangle. A new root made by an edit shares every untouched page with the old one by pointer.

## Context
Found by ceng-m1.1 (2026-10-19): ModelRoot has only a revision and sheets (crates/calc-doc-model/src/root.rs), so there are no cells for CalcEngine to borrow (ceng_m1_1__input_sharing) and nowhere for CalcDoc to load cells into (cdoc-m1.2). Plan 2.3, 3.1 and 3.2 (page boundaries and sharing). Library: calc-doc-model only. Applying authored operations (cdoc-m0.1's operation codec) to the pages is in scope: a SetCell-style operation produces a new root that shares untouched pages.

## Do
- Add sparse cell pages to ModelRoot, with page boundaries per plan 3.2, Arc-shared and immutable.
- Add borrowed reads for one cell and for a sheet's or rectangle's occupied cells, in row-major order.
- Apply the existing authored cell operations to produce a new root that shares untouched pages.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-73yy --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-73yy --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-73yy --platform wasm --require-all
```
`dc_73yy__page_sharing`: a one-cell change through the operation route leaves every untouched page pointer-identical between the old and new roots, the changed page is new, and borrowed reads of both roots return the expected inputs. Case names follow `<bead>__<case>`, registered in the owning package's acceptance.json.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox.

## Out of scope
Stable row and column slot identities and order-statistic axis maps (cdoc-m4.1 builds them on these pages, not as a second page implementation); loading cells from xlsx (cdoc-m1.2).

title: Add a calc-doc-model layering rule to the dependencies check
description:
## Outcome
The accept-time dependencies check enforces plan 1.3 for calc-doc-model: its resolved dependency closure contains no calc-engine, calc-fml, calc-host or calc-doc on any shipped target.

## Context
Follow-up of cdoc-m0.1 (2026-10-15, round-1 judge). tools/xtask/architecture.json has layering rules for calc-func, calc-fml, calc-engine, dna-onecalc and dna-calc, but none for calc-doc-model. Only cdoc-m0.1's case cdoc_m0_1__no_engine_dependency checks the model's closure, by walking the committed Cargo.lock, and that case runs only for cdoc-m0.1's own acceptance. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask).

## Do
Add a closure rule for calc-doc-model that forbids calc-engine, calc-fml, calc-host and calc-doc, with plan 1.3 as its reason. Extend infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency with a scenario that plants calc-doc-model -> calc-fml and expects the rule's line. Keep every other rule unchanged.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform linux --require-all
```
The new scenario fails the run with the calc-doc-model rule's line, and every closed bead's acceptance still passes.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Other packages' rules.
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-19, DnaCalc clone, infra lane):
- Files: tools/xtask/architecture.json (the new rule) and tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_3.rs (the scenario). Nothing else, except AGENTS.md if it lists the layering rules.
- The rule: package calc-doc-model, scope closure, forbidden calc-engine, calc-fml, calc-host and calc-doc, with plan 1.3 as its reason. Every other rule stays byte-identical.
- The scenario: infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency already generates one scenario per rule in architecture.json, so a rule deleted from the file would take its scenario with it and the case would still pass. The calc-doc-model scenario must therefore not depend on the rule being present: the case names the pair calc-doc-model -> calc-fml itself, plants that edge in its copy and expects the rule's own line ("calc-doc-model has in its dependency closure calc-fml (plan 1.3..."). It fails when the rule is missing from architecture.json, or when its forbidden list loses calc-fml.
- Check: removing the rule, or calc-fml from it, turns infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency red; the case transcript quotes the planted scenario's outcome.
- Every closed bead's acceptance is re-run on the clean tree before the push.
- Class: refuters and judge at xhigh effort, because this is an architecture check that other lanes rely on.

title: CalcVBA JIT: Abs/CVErr/Hex/Oct/Str of a Variant and Not of a Double/String/Currency constant decline the module
description:
The JIT declines a whole module when it meets one of these with a Variant (or other non-scalar) argument, so such modules run only on VM3:
- CallExtern Abs, CVErr, Hex, Oct, Str with a Variant argument (the scalar-unary shapes accept only typed scalars; e.g. `Abs(w)` with w As Variant: "M4-4 CallExtern Abs(...) subset lowers only supported ByVal scalar arguments").
- Not of a Double, String or Currency constant (`Not 1.5`: "i32 operand not lowered in M4-4: Const(F64(...))").
Found 2026-11-16 by probes temp/variant-layout-probe/ops13 (OpsProbe, LogProbe). Route these through the generic library invoke (rt_jit_lib_invoke_to_slot) or the Variant Not helper, as other Variant arguments are, and run the full probes on the JIT.

title: Scope goal: distributed, billion-node, typed and debuggable computation on Excel formulas
description:
## Outcome
DNA Calc stays based on Excel formulas, Excel functions and Excel's extensibility (LAMBDA, UDFs, add-ins). On that base it also offers what the owner's reference platform offers (Jane Street's Webs, a distributed, spreadsheet-like computation platform):
1. Distributed computation of one calculation domain across machines.
2. Incremental recomputation that scales to billions of nodes and edges, with recalculation work proportional to what changed.
3. Strong typing and rich data structures beyond traditional spreadsheet values, while the formula language stays Excel's.
4. Computations defined and edited both from Rust and from a web interface, through the same host route.
5. A formula debugger in the web interface that shows how a formula evaluated, on the one evaluator.
6. Performance at that scale, recorded with named scale workloads.

## Context
Recorded at the owner's request (2026-10-17) as a further scope goal. It is not part of the first version as plan section 11.2 and the plan header define it, and recording it changes no plan decision. The owner decides its placement (Owner questions below). The read-only mapping workflow wf_a31948f5-14a (2026-10-17) compared the goal with the plan, the tracker and the code; its findings follow.

Groundwork that exists:
- Engine state is supplied by the caller, and recalculation runs in budgeted steps (plan 2.2). Values, plans and input snapshots are immutable, Arc-shared and Send + Sync, and later frame-level parallelism against one snapshot is described (plan 3.5; cfunc_m0_1__send_sync).
- An evaluation step can request a dependency that is not ready, or yield (plan 2.2, 6.2). Async completions, pending-result tokens and external updates are versioned session operations (plan 8.8; cfml-m4.3, ceng-m4.6, chost-m4.11). Function metadata declares volatility, thread safety and async (cfunc-m4.1).
- Graph nodes exist only for formulas and participants, never for every coordinate. Ranges become interval edges, scheduling uses a ready queue with prerequisite counts and SCC condensation, an edit copies only bounded pages, and plans are shared across instances (plan 3.2, 4.1, 6.1, 6.2). Structural counters check all of this (infra-m7.8).
- Fast is deterministic across platforms, with identical effect tapes and bits (plan 5.4), so distributed results can be required to replay.
- The operation wire codec is versioned and exact, and names sheets by document-stable SheetKeys (cdoc-m0.1).
- Host dispatch is the one route for every caller, automation included (plan 2.2; chost-m4.12). Auditing must instrument the one evaluator (chost-m6.3), which is what a debugger needs.

Plan decisions the goal cuts across (owner decisions):
- One evaluator and one graph. Each workbook's mutation and calculation lane is serial, and no second parallel graph or evaluator is prebuilt in this phase (honesty rule 5; plan 3.5). Section 6 is the single-threaded reference strategy. Later strategies are admitted only behind the same operations and evaluator, checked by the differential twin (plan 6.5; ceng-m7.1). Distribution therefore has to be one graph partitioned under one ordered commit authority per domain (plan 3.3). It cannot be federated engines that exchange values in rounds (plan 6.1; ceng-m3.9).
- Excel only, with one formula language and no second DSL (executive decision; plan 4.2). Types must therefore be Excel's own (richData, entity and linked data types) or have an Excel-visible projection. A Rust definition API must produce Excel formulas, defined names and registered functions, because a computation lives in a cell or a defined name (plan header; 8.2).
- Persistence is xlsx with no sidecar, inside Excel's fixed grid (plan 8.2; calc-value grid bounds), so billions of nodes means many sheets, names or workbooks.
- No performance targets: measurements are recorded without thresholds, and a number is never called fast (plan header, 5.4, 10.4, 10.5; work prompt honesty inventory).
- Fast forbids uncontrolled reassociation (plan 5.4), so parallel or distributed reductions must keep a fixed order to stay replayable. Exact is native x86-64 only (plan 5.2).
- Portable packages cannot import networking (plan 1.3; os-imports check), so transport belongs in a native-only package under platform/.
- The browser hosts its own engine in a wasm32 worker (plan 3.5; dnacalc-m2.1). A web interface onto a shared or remote computation is a new host mode the plan does not describe.

Foreclosure risks in code that exists or comes next, cheapest to decide now:
- calc-value IDs (cfunc-m0.1, closed) are a u32 slot plus a u32 generation, which caps one workbook at about 4.29 billion node slots; the plan's sketch had u64. Slots live in a dense Vec, and calc-value declares no cargo features, so widening later breaks every consumer (crates/calc-value/src/id.rs).
- IDs are unique per allocator only, and NodeId has no document-stable key. Callable identity is a process-local Arc (crates/calc-value/src/value.rs). Cross-machine node and LAMBDA identity need a design.
- CoreValue is an exhaustive enum with no extension slot, and the 21 function-family ports will match on it. ArrayShape is usize, which is 32 bits on wasm32.
- ceng-m1.1 (the next engine bead) decides whether input pages are reached by in-process borrows or through a page-handle interface a remote partition could serve.
- cfml-m1.3 (a bottleneck bead) decides the plan and frame layout. Without an observation hook and a source-span map, a step debugger later means changing the evaluator. chost-m6.3 relies on a CalcFml trace policy that no bead owns.
- cfunc-m3.23 and cfunc-m3.4 decide the reduction order of aggregates under Fast.
- dnacalc-m2.1 decides whether its transport is independent of where the host runs.
- RecalcFacts is whole per-generation vectors (plan 2.2). AuthoredRevision is one u64 counter with one base per batch, which means one writer. ModelRoot handles sheets linearly (cdoc-m0.1), which is harmless at Excel's sheet counts.

## Do
An epic holds no work. Once the owner places this goal, a planning bead derives its child beads (as infra-m3.20 to infra-m3.24 do) and attaches them at these points:
- ceng-m7.1's strategy layer;
- ceng-m3.9's calculation domain;
- the async route of cfml-m4.3 and ceng-m4.6;
- dnacalc-m2.1's transport and a native-only transport package under platform/;
- chost-m4.12's programmatic route;
- auditing in chost-m6.3 and dnacalc-m6.19;
- infra-m7.8's named workloads;
- typed values in cdoc-m3.4, infra-m3.23 and cfunc-m3.19.

## Owner questions
1. Placement: a phase after the first version (after infra-m8.2), or do parts of it enter earlier?
2. ID width: keep calc-value's u32 slots, or widen them to u64 before cdoc-m0.1 closes and before ceng-m1.1 builds on them?
3. Typed values: exactly Excel's own data types, so that Excel opens them, or a DNA extension? And does CoreValue gain an extension slot now?
4. Performance: keep recorded workloads without thresholds, or set targets for named scale workloads? Targets would lift a plan rule.
5. Determinism: must parallel and distributed results stay bit-identical to the serial reference? A yes fixes the reduction order.
6. Anchoring: may a Rust-defined computation exist without a cell or defined-name anchor? The plan header and section 8.2 say no today.
7. Persistence: must every computation still open in Excel, or is a second store admitted for billion-node graphs?
8. Debugger timing: does formula auditing (chost-m6.3, M6, P3) move earlier, and which bead owns the CalcFml trace policy?

## Out of scope
Any change to the first version's scope, to the plan text or to build_plan.py until the owner rules on the questions above.
notes:
Owner rulings (2026-10-18):
- Question 2, ID width, is answered with option 1. calc-value keeps its 32-bit slots, and no ID is widened. Excel-size workbooks sit two to three orders of magnitude below the cap of about 4.29 billion slots per kind per workbook, and memory runs out long before that. Compact 32-bit slots keep the engine's edge lists small. If this goal is ever placed, scale beyond one process comes from partitioning the graph: each partition has its own allocator and graph, and a cross-partition reference is a (partition, NodeId) pair. A distributed graph needs that layer whatever the slot width.
- Scope guard: no work items and no design go down this goal's path beyond what Excel scope needs. The epic stays deferred. No bead adds Webs-specific abstractions, interfaces, APIs, workloads or extension slots, such as remote page access, a remote host transport, partition-aware IDs, DNA-only typed values or billion-node workloads, unless the owner places this epic. The notes on the attachment beads were narrowed to Excel-scope choices on the same day.

title: calc-func's x87 route has no wasm32 form: 15 Excel-bit tests fail in the browser
description:
## Outcome
calc-func's Excel-bit kernels give Excel's bits in the browser (wasm32) as they do on x86_64, so DNA OneCalc and DNA Calc in the browser publish the values Excel does.

## Found by
dc-msg, running calc-func's unit tests in Chrome and Firefox. `excel_numeric` reproduces Excel through the x87 CRT sequences (`x87.rs`, inline x87 assembly), which exist only on x86_64. On wasm32 every entry point takes its portable fallback (`powf`, `atan`, the glibc-2.29 exp/log port), which the module docs call "not bit-exact".

## Measured
In Chrome, 15 of calc-func's lib tests that pin live-Excel bits fail by one ULP (or by a count of pins), all through x87-route entry points: BINOM k=n and NEGBINOM k=0 (pow chain), BESSELY, BESSELJ, XNPV, PRICE, DURATION, POWER (fractional and negative-base reciprocal roots), T.INV.2T df=1 (tan), T.DIST df=2 pdf (pow chain), RRI (2 tests), NPER, NOMINAL. They are marked `Native-only:` with this bead named; `cargo xtask check --wasm` prints them per package.

## Do
- Give the x87 route a wasm32 form that reproduces the x86_64 bits (a software form of the x87 sequences the CRT runs, or of what Excel computes at these sites), measured against the x86_64 route over the pinned rows and a large sample.
- Then turn the 15 tests back to the native/browser attribute pair.
- dc-sbo (the `f64::powf` sites) is the neighbouring gap; the two may share a portable pow.
notes: Three more calc-func lib tests were already compiled only on x86_64 for the same reason (atan_retains_extended_inverse_angle_and_pi, gammaln stirling_ln87_dr_matches_current_build_hits_and_keeps_two_open, normal_dist_common phi_matches_live_excel_pinned_witnesses); dc-msg marks them `Native-only:` with this bead too, so 18 tests name dc-8dg.
close_reason: calc-func's Excel-bit kernels give Excel's bits in the browser: the x87 route has a software form (soft87.rs) that matches the hardware exactly for + - * /, sqrt, rounding, scaling, remainder and stores (0 differences in 100,000 random cases per operation under six control words; 0 in 400,000 double-rounded pairs), and runs each transcendental chain written once on hardware (x86_64) or in software (elsewhere), differing from the hardware in 0-85 per 1,000,000 random arguments per chain because the CPU microcode for F2XM1, FPTAN, FYL2X, FSIN, FCOS, FPATAN does not round exactly (no reproducible pattern found). Live-Excel witnesses in software: EXP 136 of 136, LN 95 of 113 (the 18 misses are 1 ulp and named by the test). 17 of the 18 tests that named dc-8dg run in Chrome and Firefox again. Evidence: cargo xtask check --wasm passed (calc-func 483 in both browsers, 16 native-only with reasons); catalogue oracle 5,998 of 6,309 identical cell for cell on the hardware and software routes (soft-x87 feature); Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272 on both routes. Commits 98046b0, f42ecc7. Still open: the microcode residue; platform libm calls (dc-ba bead filed alongside); software cost about 64 ns per arithmetic operation and 1-2.5 us per transcendental chain natively.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text: Function exactness lane, 2026-10-25 (98046b0): the x87 chains run in the browser. excel_numeric/soft87.rs is the x87 in software (80-bit format; FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV/FSQRT/FRNDINT/FSCALE/FPREM1 and the binary64 store exact under every control word; ROM constants equal the hardware's; F2XM1/FYL2X/FPATAN/FSIN/FCOS/FPTAN round the exact value once). Each chain is written once over an Fpu trait: x86_64 runs the hardware, wasm32 the software x87 (feature soft-x87 runs it on x86_64 for measurement). Measured against the hardware (Ryzen 7 4800H): exact operations 0 differences in 100,000 per operation and control word; double-rounded + - * / and reciprocal 0 in 400,000 pairs each; binary64 chain results per 1,000,000 random arguments: EXP 0, ATAN reduced 0, staged SQRT 0, chopped EXP 1, SIN 3, COS 2, ATAN 3, BINOM exp 3, LOG10 9, LN 11, pow chain 13, TAN 16, GEOMEAN root 25, direct pow 85 (the residue is the hardware microcode: F2XM1 differs from the exactly rounded value at 3.3% of 64-bit results, FYL2X 2.1%, FPTAN 2.9%, FSIN 1.5%, FCOS 0.36%, FPATAN 0.11%). Live-Excel witnesses in software: EXP 136 of 136, LN 95 of 113 (18 named in the test, each a hardware FYL2X result that differs from the exactly rounded one). Catalogue oracle cell for cell identical on both routes (pass 5,998 of 6,309; fail 311 = 269 mismatched + 42 refused); Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272 on both. 17 of the 18 tests naming this bead run in Chrome and Firefox; BESSELY stays native-only for f64::ln (platform libm, dc-sbo). cargo xtask check --wasm: calc-func 481 in the browsers, 16 native-only. Still open: the microcode residue above. Not closed: the owner closes.

description:

calc-func's catalogue holds OxFunc's math and trigonometry (the rest of the family), rounding remainder, SUBTOTAL and AGGREGATE, descriptive statistics and the probability distributions, engineering (bases, bits, complex numbers, Bessel, ERF) and random-number functions, each computing through calc_func::invoke, with OxFunc's tests ported.

title: Keep infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency's OS-binding scenarios independent of the stand-in package's dependents
description:
## Outcome
infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency passes on a workspace in which portable packages depend on calc-value, because its OS-binding scenarios no longer depend on which packages happen to depend on the package that carries the stand-in crate.

## Context
Prerequisite of cfunc-m0.1's close (2026-10-15). cfunc-m0.1 adds calc-func's dependency on calc-value. The OS-binding scenarios of infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_3.rs, the `binding` table near line 1655) attach a stand-in `winapi` crate to crates/calc-value and expect exactly calc-value's lines. With the new edge, the check also reports, correctly, that portable calc-func has winapi in its wasm32-unknown-unknown closure, so os-binding-direct and os-binding-transitive each gain one line and the case fails ('failures: 2', round-3 refuter of cfunc-m0.1). The check is right; the expectation is too narrow. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask).

## Do
Attach the stand-in to a portable package that no workspace member may depend on, such as apps/dna-onecalc, or compute the expected lines from the copy's resolved metadata (the stand-in package plus each portable package whose closure reaches it). In either case, assert that every line the check prints names a package whose closure really contains the stand-in. Keep every other scenario of the case unchanged.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform linux --require-all
```
infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency passes on master after cfunc-m0.1's build commit, and its os-binding scenarios still fail when the deny-listed crate is present.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Changing the os-imports check itself.
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-15):
- The fix stays inside tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_3.rs; the os-imports check itself does not change.
- Attach the stand-in winapi and shim crates to apps/dna-onecalc, a portable package that no workspace member may depend on: a library or application depending on OneCalc would break plan 2.1's diagram. Then the expectation stays exactly one package's lines. Each scenario also asserts that every line the check prints names dna-onecalc, so a line about any other package fails the case.
- Proof: the case passes at HEAD 98f99fd (calc-func depends on calc-value) through `cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all`, and Linux runs after the push. The scenarios still fail when the deny-listed crate is present (the case asserts exit 1 and the exact lines).
close_reason:
Product status: infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency passes again with calc-func depending on calc-value. Its OS-binding stand-in sits on apps/dna-onecalc, which no member depends on, and each scenario checks that from the copy's resolved metadata. The os-imports check is unchanged.
Evidence: commit 1416d1c, pushed after cfunc-m0.1's 98f99fd.
- Windows: cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all exit 0, "2 selected, 2 passed ... architecture checks 7/7 passed" (accept-receipts/infra-m0.3/windows.json).
- Linux, in the WSL clone at 1416d1c: cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform linux --require-all exit 0, "ACCEPT passed infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency" (accept-receipts/infra-m0.3/linux.json).
- fmt and clippy -D warnings exit 0.
- Probes failed the case when the check's wasm32 closure was emptied ("failures: 2") and when every line named calc-value ("failures: 4"). With the holder set to calc-value, the precondition and the resolved-metadata check also failed ("failures: 7"). Logs are under target/accept/dc-8gn8/.
- CI push run 38724812987 is green.
Still open: dc-tj29, for propagation between workspace members and native-only dependents. The "every line names the holder" assertion repeats the exact-lines and resolved-metadata assertions and protects nothing they miss.

title: One code-execution policy across runtimes (VBA, XLL, COM, coming JavaScript add-ins)
description: Owner 2026-11-11: our VBA security is a refinement of Excel's model, not a copy: we can mirror Excel and block, allow (same as Excel allows; signing etc. to be decided), or run in our Safe mode (dc-10un). JavaScript add-in support starts soon. Manage development, triage, corpus and test policies and the in-app settings in one combined way, even where details differ between runtimes. Write docs/architecture/CODE_EXECUTION_POLICY.md: the three app levels (Off, Safe, Unguarded; dc-15dk), the static triage (suspect or not; public corpora vs web-harvested one notch stricter; own code runs), review-and-approve for unguarded execution of flagged files, the capability vocabulary shared across runtimes (fs.read, fs.write, process, env, settings, ffi, com.activate, ui.keys, network), per-runtime notes (VBA: CalcVBA PolicyHost; XLL/COM native code: no Safe mode possible, source-built only for harvested add-ins; JavaScript: sandboxed by its host), signing as an open item. title: CalcVBA: run VBA on Windows, macOS, Linux and wasm with known results (dialects, modes, shims, report)
description:
Design: CalcVBA docs/design/portability.md. Matrix: conformance/excel-measurements/vba-library/portability-matrix.tsv (make_portability_matrix.py).
- **Two dialects:** Windows Excel VBA and Mac Excel VBA, each checked against its own Excel.
- **Four kinds of host:** Windows, macOS, Linux and WebAssembly (WASI and browser).
- **The matrix:** every library procedure, statement and language feature, with a class, the Mac dialect difference, a per-host verdict (native, model, shim, host, replace, reject) and what CalcVBA does today.
- **Goal:** before running, know whether a project gives the answers of the Excel it was written for on this host; then shim it, replace it, or reject it at load with the reason.
- **Related:** the library check dc-q6brh, including the locale (dc-q6brh.6) and maths (dc-q6brh.112) models.

title: CalcVBA in the browser: worker execution, synchronous UI channel, virtual file system, storage
description:
The WasmBrowserSandbox profile has no file system, process, dynamic linking or UI.
- **Blocking:** VBA is synchronous and the main thread cannot block, so run VBA in a Web Worker. MsgBox and InputBox go to the page through a synchronous channel (SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics.wait; needs cross-origin isolation). Without the channel, projects that use modal UI are rejected for the browser.
- **Files:** the path map onto a virtual file system (in memory, or the origin-private file system), with import and export through the page.
- **Settings:** IndexedDB.
- **Time:** the clock from Date.now; the time zone and locale from the project, falling back to the browser's.
- **Execution:** VM3 only.
- **Rejected:** Shell, Declare (bar emulations), COM (bar portable classes), SendKeys, AppActivate.
- **Done:** the probes pass in a headless browser in faithful mode.

title: CalcVBA shim: path map, case-insensitive lookup and file attributes (macOS, Linux, WASI, browser)
description:
Design note section 6. A per-project path map:
- **Windows dialect:** drive letters to roots, UNC to mounts, backslash to /.
- **Mac dialect:** POSIX paths under mapped roots.
- **Roots per host:** real folders on macOS and Linux, preopened directories on WASI, the virtual file system in the browser (in memory or the origin-private file system).

CurDir reports the dialect's form, and an unmapped drive raises 76. Names resolve case-insensitively, and two names differing only in case are an error. An attribute store (xattr or sidecar) holds hidden/system/archive.

Covers Open, Kill, Dir, MkDir, RmDir, ChDir, ChDrive, FileCopy, Name, FileLen and FileDateTime. Done: the vba-library file-system probes give the reference answers on every non-native host.

title: Shared result states, useful shell and accessible feedback
description:
Context: docs/plan/UI_REVIEW.md and architecture sections 8.7 and 9.

Done when every Calc skin can show literal, calculated, file cache, stale, pending, refused and worksheet-error states with text or shape cues; pending work and worker failure have visible status; selecting a refusal opens its exact reason, owner if supplied by the backend, and a recovery action without inventing ownership. A calculated count is never labelled matched Excel. Move iteration limits, revision IDs, intent counts, wasm memory and timings into a labelled diagnostics disclosure. At 390, 1024 and 1440 pixels commands, sheet tabs, status and active editor remain reachable. Label controls, expose bounded grid/tree semantics and keyboard exit/focus restoration, announce result/error changes, preserve dirty work on New/Open, and distinguish download started from durable save. Use original Strand tokens/assets; document keyboard, accessibility-tree and contrast checks in both browsers.

Acceptance: extend the existing app smoke/fixtures and canonical host route; record screenshots outside git, actual browser results and remaining limitations. Original Strand look; no Microsoft icons, artwork or trade dress.
notes:
Users can distinguish literal, calculated, file cache, stale, pending, refused and worksheet-error results in every skin, inspect the exact refusal with an owner only from typed backend data, and use an edit/calculate recovery action. Worker startup, outstanding requests and failure are visible; failed workers drain callbacks without replacing the workbook. Technical state sits in labelled diagnostics. Shared drafts and Notebook drafts survive skin changes; New/Open require an explicit discard decision when work is dirty, empty undo/redo is disabled, and a download is described without claiming durable storage. F6 region movement, sheet-tab keys, bounded grid/tree semantics, named controls and result announcements work at 390/1024/1440 CSS pixels with original Strand tokens and strict CSP.

Implementation extends existing worker messages and the shared formula result presentation; no parallel evaluator. Existing app smoke checks computed WebDriver roles/names, rendered active descendants, bounded semantic windows, reachable controls, state-text contrast >=4.5 in light/dark/high-contrast themes, real generated downloads/imports and real Worker startup failure on a tool-only server. Firefox 390px uses standard WebDriver BiDi viewport resizing; its desktop window has a 500px minimum. The existing package-part replacement helper now accepts compressed packages and checks CRC/length; no oracle/golden values or captures were changed.

Merged-tree browser evidence in ~/codex-runs/ui-3-*.log: Calc 149/149 and OneCalc 27/27 per Chrome and Firefox; portable tests 16 shared UI + 70 Calc library + 4 workbook in each browser, zero ignored. Native/wasm dependency ceiling passed (only that sweep step, not a full sweep). Corpus before/after unchanged: 21 workbooks compared, 19284/20030 matched (96.27%); 659 failures = 652 mismatched + 6 refused + 1 failed/missing; 73 external-link and 14 circular-rule cells reported separately, never passes; zero awaiting capture. Linux cargo xtask check passed: 1175 passed, zero failed, three existing ignored across 65 harnesses of 15 packages (ui-3-check-final.log). Screenshots: 36 before and 36 after at 1440x1000, 1024x768, 390x844 plus 36 exploratory previews under ~/codex-runs/ui-shots/slice-3-*.png. Final after observations: zero page faults, zero horizontal document overflow. Still open: Windows per-commit verification and live Excel unavailable on this Linux host; actual screen-reader speech and native IME devices are not certified by synthetic events or WebDriver tree checks. Calculation mode is a session setting: saved packages retain the opened file mode declaration; Settings now says this explicitly, and the file-cache smoke prepares an explicitly manual input rather than claiming download persistence parity. Native IME/caret/text-undo measurements from .2 remain open. Full skin-specific authoring remains in .10-.15. The shipping worker emits bounded binary TileBatch fragments separately from controls, with workbook/transaction identity, base/next ordering, dictionary and geometry/style epochs, explicit removals and the real engine publication identity. The portable RenderPlan supplies current painting, bounded semantic rows and read-only browser inspection. title: CalcVBA Windows: native_breadth fails since engine Dictionary became public (check.ps1 red)
description:
Windows-only master regression since CalcVBA 72b6d67d3 (dc-tey4.4, "public engine Dictionary"): `cargo test -p calcvba-build --test native_breadth` fails (`conformance_bodies_agree_in_vm3_jit_and_aot`), so `./scripts/check.ps1` fails on Windows. Not seen on the Linux lane because the test is `cfg(windows, x86_64)`.

Cause (read and probed 2026-11-13 at 219403627): 72b6d67d3 set `vb_exposed = true` on the engine's VBA-source Scripting.Dictionary class (calcvba-symbol/src/scripting.rs:300-310). Native-library builds now compile that class's procedures through the AOT lane, which refuses them: first `Class_Initialize` (`ReDim pKeys(0 To 7)` on a class field lowers through a Variant temp; calcvba-jit/src/native.rs:513-518 admits only Array-typed ArrayRedim destinations), then `Insert` (`FieldArraySet` unsupported). Adding a Variant-destination redim helper (tried, reverted) gets the build through but ActivationSuite then returns "ERROR 13: Type mismatch" instead of Excel's "9:True": CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary") in a native export now reaches the engine class rather than the OS Scripting runtime.

Decide: should a Windows native export's CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary") create the OS COM object, as Excel does (then keep the engine class out of native images), or the engine class (then the AOT lane must compile the whole class: Variant-temp ReDim, FieldArraySet, ...)? Excel behaviour argues for the OS object on Windows.

Also on master at 219403627: rustfmt (9 files) and one clippy collapsible_if (calcvba-bind/src/call.rs:2955) failed; fixed in the dc-yqq0.1 commit.
close_reason: CalcVBA 27765527f: the source of Scripting.Dictionary is a choice (TypeLibResolver::dictionary_source; Engine::set_dictionary_source; Provider::with_dictionary_source). Native images use the OS Scripting runtime on Windows (owner 2026-11-13), so native exports/executables no longer compile the engine class; real-Dictionary typed-host and parity tests opt in. Interpreter lanes keep the engine class until dc-yqq0.8 (New of COM class, late-bound ByRef, metadata-less late names). Remaining unrelated Windows failures: new bead.

title: JIT declines ByRef pass of a UDT scalar field to a typed scalar parameter (riff)
description: The JIT declines a call that passes a Record (UDT) scalar field ByRef to a typed scalar parameter, e.g. `Bump(1.5!, vs(i).Z)` with `Private Function Bump(ByVal x As Single, ByRef z As Single)`: "M4-4 static call subset requires exact ByRef type match, got Variant for Single at Temp". Cause: CalcVBA calcvba-oxir elaborate/lower.rs lower_byref_place copies a compound place into a temp typed by record_field_result_ty, which is Variant for every scalar record field; the JIT's lower_static_call_arg (calcvba-jit lowering.rs) needs the exact type for a ByRef alias. VM3 runs it (copy-in, copy-out through the Variant temp). Blocks the JIT load of the riff corpus project (RiffProcessVoiceFilters); riff has no worksheet cases, so the corpus count does not move. Fix options: type the temp by the record layout's scalar field type, or have the JIT convert between a Variant temp and a typed scalar slot around the call.

title: Language and engine cases dc-10y left refused

## Outcome
The language and engine cases dc-10y left refused compute as Excel does.

## Context
dc-10y (bea7a7e) measured and implemented most of its list; these stay refused:
- OFFSET/INDIRECT lifted over an array returns an array of references: SUM adds them all, SUBTOTAL, N, SUMIF and COUNTIF lift element by element. Needs an array-of-references value.

- Cycle cells with iteration off whose only value is the file's stored one stay refused by rule (file caches never score); nothing to do unless the owner changes that rule.

title: Template files (.xltx/.xltm/.xlt) supported on par with Excel
description:
Owner direction 2026-11-04: template files supported on par with Excel.

Scope (Excel's behaviour is the reference; record it in Excel on the Windows machine where unclear):
- File formats: .xltx, .xltm (with VBA, through CalcVBA's vbaProject.bin reader and write-back), legacy .xlt read where the file layer reads .xls. Content types and the template flag in the package, so a template saved by us opens as a template in Excel and the reverse.

- Engine: a workbook created from a template calculates as Excel does on creation (volatile functions, calculation mode from the template).

Lanes: file layer (formats, flags, round trip), UI (New from template, Save As template, insert sheet), CalcVBA (.xltm VBA), Windows Excel lane (recorded answers for open/save/new behaviour).

title: Resolve _xlfn.-prefixed function names in a loaded formula to the catalogue function
description:
## Outcome
A formula loaded from a file that spells a function with Excel's file prefix (_xlfn.IFNA, _xlfn.MAXIFS, _xlfn._xlws.FILTER) compiles to the same catalogue function as its plain name, so calc_fml, calc_engine and calc_host compute it; the document keeps the file text unchanged, so a save writes the prefix back as loaded.

## Context
The first cargo xtask compare run (dc-kt3l, 2026-10-21): Default-tariff-cap-level spells IFNA as _xlfn.IFNA in 49 formulas whose results 62,786 other formula cells read, and calc_fml's compile refuses _xlfn.IFNA as UnknownFunction because it looks the spelling up as written (crates/calc-fml/src/eval/compile.rs). Every function Excel added after 2007 is stored with the prefix (MAXIFS, MINIFS, IFNA, XLOOKUP, CONCAT, FILTER), so loaded workbooks meet the same refusal. dc-552j owns the save half (adding prefixes to authored text from catalogue metadata) and converting UI text to file form; this bead takes only name resolution of the file form.

## Do
- In calc_fml's compile, resolve a call whose name carries the _xlfn. prefix, optionally followed by _xlws., by the name after the prefixes; keep the spelling as written for diagnostics; refuse as now when the plain name is not catalogued. Whether an unprefixed spelling of a prefixed function, or a prefixed spelling of a function Excel never prefixes, is accepted follows what Excel does when it loads such a file (measure it, or refuse with a typed refusal naming dc-552j).
- A case that compiles and evaluates =_xlfn.IFNA(...), =_xlfn.MAXIFS(...) (or catalogued functions that carry the prefix) through calc_fml::evaluate, and opens a generator-built package holding them through calc_host, with the cells calculated.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
_xlfn.-prefixed calls of catalogued functions compute through calc_fml::evaluate and through calc_host on a loaded package; an unknown prefixed name is still refused as UnknownFunction with its spelling.

## Out of scope
Adding prefixes on save, error constants on save, UI text conversion (dc-552j).

title: CalcFunc for Python, .NET and JavaScript: Excel-exact function libraries generated from the catalogue, published from the handbook
CalcFunc bindings: shared design (boundary, metadata, value model, hard cases, profiles)
description:
Write a design note, docs/design/calcfunc-bindings.md, for the shared layer under the Python, .NET and JavaScript libraries, then the follow-up beads. The note must settle these questions, with a recommendation for each.

1. Boundary
   - Options: one C ABI crate (calc-func-ffi) generated from the catalogue, used by .NET through P/Invoke and by Python through cffi; or PyO3 for Python, with the C ABI only for .NET.
   - JavaScript goes through wasm-bindgen over the soft-x87 wasm build, for Node and browsers.
   - Settle ownership of strings and arrays across the boundary. Panics never cross it.
   - Thread safety: CalcFunc calls are pure, so release the GIL and keep no global state.

2. Metadata
   - What calc-catalogue records today: names, arity, argument kinds (number, text, logical, reference, array), optional and repeating arguments, volatility, array lifting, return shape.
   - What a typed API still needs: reference-versus-value semantics per argument, lifting per argument, default values, and which functions are context-bound.
   - Add the missing fields to the catalogue itself, never a side table (extend, never duplicate).

3. Value model
   - number, text, logical;
   - errors: #N/A, #VALUE! and the rest, including #SPILL! and #CALC!;
   - empty cell versus missing argument: PMT(r,n,pv,,1) is not PMT(r,n,pv,0,1);
   - 2-D arrays with mixed element types;
   - -0.0, NaN payloads, subnormals.

   Errors come back as values by default; raising them is an option.

4. Difficult cases, each with a decision
   - Reference semantics. SUM(A1:A3) ignores text and logicals in a range, but SUM("3", TRUE) coerces them when given directly. The API needs a Range (reference) value distinct from a literal array; COUNT, AVERAGE, MATCH, the IFS family and SUMPRODUCT treat the two differently.
   - Implicit intersection and array lifting: scalar functions applied element-wise to arrays, 1xN broadcast against Nx1, spill shapes.
   - Locale. Text-to-number and date coercion depend on locale (VALUE, DATEVALUE, TEXT, number formats). Use a locale profile, en-US by default.
   - Dates. The 1900 and 1904 date systems and the 1900 leap-year bug. Helpers for serial versus datetime/DateTime/Date never change the arithmetic.
   - Text:
     - UTF-16 code-unit semantics (LEN, MID, FIND on astral characters);
     - Excel collation for comparisons, MATCH, SORT and lookups;
     - the 32,767-character limit.
   - Volatile and environment functions (RAND, RANDBETWEEN, RANDARRAY, NOW, TODAY) take an injected clock and random source.
   - Functions taking LAMBDA (MAP, REDUCE, SCAN, BYROW, BYCOL, MAKEARRAY) either accept host callables or are left out.
   - Out of the function library: cell-context, workbook and host functions (ROW, COLUMN, CELL, INDIRECT, OFFSET, ISFORMULA, FORMULATEXT, INFO, RTD, WEBSERVICE, CUBE, GETPIVOTDATA, IMAGE). A later formula-level evaluator over calc-fml with a small workbook model is a separate bead.
   - Numeric fidelity: native x87 versus soft-x87.
     - Native transcendental bits differ by CPU. Soft-x87 reproduces the recorded answers everywhere.
     - The profile names the Excel build and the CPU it reproduces.
     - Default to soft-x87, so results are the same on every machine and in wasm.
   - Number-to-text publication (15 significant digits) where a function returns text from a number.

5. Profiles
   - Use the same profile identifiers as DNA Calc: Excel build, CPU, bit-exact versus a later improved mode.
   - Carry them per call or per session.

6. Verification
   - The whole witness bank and the pinned sets run through each binding and must match CalcFunc bit for bit.
   - Tests for the generated signatures, docstrings and stubs.
   - A per-function status table, generated from witness-status.tsv, ships with each package and appears on the handbook pages.

7. Packaging targets
   - Windows x64 and Linux x64 first; macOS later.
   - wasm (npm, Pyodide, Blazor) from the soft-x87 build.
close_reason: Wrote docs/design/calcfunc-bindings.md for Python, .NET and JavaScript. Staged checks verified 0 -> 1 design document and 10/10 relative source links. Docs-only; Cargo unavailable and no runtime or witness run. Package implementation and runtime verification remain with dc-dfl.2.2/.3/.4, handbook publication with dc-dfl.2.5, per-parameter lifting with dc-dfl.2.6, and the separate formula API with dc-dfl.2.7.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text:
Owner thought 2026-11-23 (not a directive): two functions, e.g. SUM and SUMRANGE. Coordinator notes for the design:
- Per-function variants work for the repeating-argument aggregates (SUM, COUNT, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, AND, OR), where every argument takes the same kind. They do not scale to mixed calls such as SUM(range, "3"), which would need one variant per combination of argument kinds.
- Names that could clash with Excel functions should be avoided; if variants are made, use a namespace (xl.SUM against xl.range.SUM).
- Alternative worth weighing: plain containers (lists, numpy arrays, DataFrame columns) default to range semantics, since that is what data from cells is. Scalars stay literal. Values returned by the library come back tagged as Excel arrays, so feeding one function result into another keeps array semantics. Range([[x]]) or a cell() helper covers the single-cell case.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text: Owner 2026-11-23 asked whether cell() needs an opposite. Coordinator view: yes, a small array(x) that marks a container as an Excel array (an array constant or a computed array), the same tag results carry. Rarely needed, because ranges and arrays give the same values in nearly all functions. Where they differ, Excel errors on the array: reference-only arguments (the COUNTIF/SUMIF/IFS family range argument, COUNTBLANK, the database functions, AGGREGATE functions 1-13), and ISREF says FALSE. Uses: transcribing a sheet formula with an array constant exactly, including its errors; tests; and re-tagging a result after the user has transformed it (a returned array that numpy has modified comes back plain, so it reads as a range). Count the functions where the two differ from the catalogue (ParameterClass Reference) and list them in the note.

A handbook landing page lists the three packages, their install lines and the profile notes. The handbook's llms.txt lists the packages too.

Release notes come from the same records. Nothing goes to PyPI, NuGet or npm without the owner's yes.

title: Catalogue: an explicit per-parameter lifting answer for every function (derive from existing metadata if possible)
description:
Owner 2026-11-23: sweep the CalcFunc function metadata and give each parameter an explicit flag for whether it lifts. Lifting means the function runs once per element when the parameter gets an array or range, instead of taking the array whole.

Much of this may already be recorded. calc-catalogue (crates/calc-catalogue/src/declarations.rs) has, per parameter:
- `ParameterClass`: Value / ValueOrReference / Reference;
- `EntryClass`;
- `LegacyPlace`: about thirty variants, such as ArrayAlways, AggregateAtRoot and IntersectReference.

And per entry, `EntryTraits`: lift_dynamic_references, lift_references_from, lift_computed_array, zero_lifted_blank and zero_dynamic_lifted_blank. calc-fml's eval/lift.rs and run.rs apply them.

First establish whether the per-parameter answer can be derived mechanically from those fields together with calc-fml's rules, in both dynamic-array and legacy formulas.

- If it can: add a catalogue function that derives it, for example `parameter_lifting(entry, index, mode) -> Elementwise | Whole | PerReference`. Add a test that compares it with what calc-fml actually does for every function and parameter. Generate a table, docs/reference/parameter-lifting.tsv, for the bindings and the handbook. Do not add a second stored copy (extend, never duplicate).
- If it cannot: add the missing field to Parameter, and fill it for every function from calc-fml's behaviour and recorded Excel answers. List the functions where Excel's behaviour is not yet measured in a child bead for a Windows round.

Acceptance:
- Every catalogue function and parameter has a lifting answer for both modes.
- The test fails if calc-fml and the declared answer ever disagree.
- The table lists its counts: lifting parameters, whole parameters, per-reference parameters, and unmeasured ones.
close_reason: Derived catalogue lifting by input origin and formula placement for all 548 entries and 19,178 call positions, including repeated positions and lazy branches. The generated TSV has 345,204 decisions: 12,164 elementwise, 2,048 conditional elementwise, 203,488 whole, 3,120 per-reference, and 12,335 unmeasured, plus explicit intersection, rejection and special-form outcomes. CalcFml agreed on 326,304 held-call decisions. Linux cargo xtask check --dependents passed 3,404 tests with 0 failures on base 7c13bcc1, after excluding nine VBA corpus-execution cases per lane instruction and serializing xtask self-tests. Before and after the lifting changes, 156 retained oracle workbooks had 78,344 matches out of 78,390 cells (99.94%) and 46 failures (27 mismatched, 0 refused, 5 failed or missing, 14 circular-rule). Unmeasured legacy and held-reference behavior stays with dc-b1l; deferred entries with dc-fetch-f0tp and dc-nk93. Claim commit 7a11fb31; implementation, tests and table in this commit.

title: DTC one-cell edit and memory against Excel; confirm Excel's CalculateFull timing
description:
## Outcome
DNA Calc's one-cell edit and its memory on the DTC model are no worse than Excel's, measured with cargo xtask bench; and Excel's own timings in the bench are shown to measure what they claim.

## Context
dc-10d9 (bdf33b3, C:\Work\DnaCalc\corpus\perf\final-bdf33b3\bench.md): DTC one-cell edit DNA 0.896 s vs Excel 0.222 s ('3g CPIH'!C328, 83,547 of 165,810 formulas recalculated); peak working set DNA 424 MB vs Excel 332 MB (about 230 MB of Excel's is an empty instance). Excel's CalculateFull measured 0.061 s on DTC, faster than its own one-cell edit (0.222 s) and 57x faster than its CalculateFullRebuild (3.481 s); that ordering is unexplained.

## Do
- First confirm the Excel figures: time CalculateFull with multithreaded calculation off on the script's own instance, check that every formula really recalculated (for example a volatile counter cell or CalculationState and a changed precedent), and record per-thread cost for both systems.
- Then cut DNA Calc's edit cost: reads of results the recalculation does not recompute (tree lookup), range reads through the cell walker, IF and SUM, the ready queue; and the INDIRECT reach on the benchmark sheets that widens the dirty set.
- Cut DTC peak memory.

## Acceptance
cargo xtask bench before/after medians on all three Ofgem workbooks; Ofgem stays 209,272 of 209,272.

title: Read digit-bearing text that cannot be a number, date or time as text, so labels such as 2016-17 Winter compute
description:
## Outcome
calc_func decides, for digit-bearing text that Excel's en-US number, date and time recognition cannot read (for example "2016-17 Winter" or "Q1 2016"), that it is not a number, so criteria, comparisons and coercions over such labels compute instead of being refused; text the rule cannot decide stays refused as not modelled.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison (dc-3t1b): refuter 2 of cfunc-m3.5 counted 1,748 criteria in Annex-4 built as "op"&cell over digit-bearing labels such as "2016-17 Winter". crates/calc-func/src/coerce.rs number_text refuses any text holding a digit outside the plain decimal form (owner NUMBER_TEXT, cfml-m2.6), and the conditional kernels refuse the call. cfml-m2.6 owns the whole number-text service (dates, times, fractions, currency, locales); this bead takes only the negative verdict that is certain.

## Do
- Measure in Excel on this machine which digit-bearing forms en-US Excel reads as numbers (VALUE over a generated list: month names and abbreviations, numeric dates with / and -, times with : and AM/PM, fractions, percent, currency, grouped digits, parenthesised negatives, exponents, weekday names), and write the rule from that: text holding a letter run that none of those forms accepts is not a number. Everything else outside the plain decimal form stays not modelled.
- Read-only scan of the three Ofgem workbooks (outside the repository, licence unverified: commit counts only, no cell text): the distinct digit-bearing texts in cells that criteria ranges cover and in the cells "op"&cell criteria name, and how many the rule decides.
- Narrow the NUMBER_TEXT owner in calc-func's acceptance tables to what still refuses; note on cfml-m2.6.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
Rows through calc_func::invoke (a comparison, a coercion such as "2016-17 Winter"+0, and a COUNTIF or SUMIF criterion over such labels): each decided row's result equals Excel's, measured on this machine and compared through calc_verdict once the capture route works (not_run with MissingCapture until then); undecided forms (a date with a month name, a time, a fraction) stay refused.

## Out of scope
Reading dates, times, fractions, currency or grouped digits as numbers (cfml-m2.6).
close_reason: Product status: calc_func reads printable-ASCII text holding a digit as not a number when it also holds a run of ASCII letters outside the measured list (a month name or a prefix of one with 3 or more letters, A, P, AM, PM, E, and R, en-ZA's currency symbol): "2016-17 Winter"+0 is #VALUE!, the criterion "=2016-17 Winter" asks for text, a label cell does not meet = a number, and COUNTIF, COUNTIFS, SUMIF, SUMIFS, AVERAGEIF, AVERAGEIFS, MAXIFS and MINIFS over such labels compute. Undecided text (dates with month names, times, fractions, R amounts, grouped digits, non-ASCII text) stays refused under cfml-m2.6. The certainty is for en-ZA as measured (user culture en-ZA, country setting 27, Excel 16.0 build 20430); calc_func's context carries no locale, and other locales are cfml-m2.6's (its corrected note names the words). Against Excel's capture of the oracle workbook: calculated 699 of 1,144, matched 699, 0 mismatched; 409 not modelled under cfml-m2.6; the 1,056 generated texts: 660 decided, all #VALUE! in Excel; 396 undecided (1e5 reads as 100000; of the other 395, Excel reads 81 as numbers and gives #VALUE! for 314); VALUE equals +0 on the 36 texts read. Ofgem Annex-4: the rule decides all 1,748 "="&cell label criteria and all 31 distinct digit-bearing texts in its criteria ranges. Orchestrator ruling (recorded on this bead): the end-to-end "="&cell case through calc-fml is dc-3t1b's. Evidence: build commit 3662bb0; cargo xtask accept --id dc-e00t --platform windows --require-all (started 2026-10-21T17:15:47Z at fa43827, 2/2) and --platform wasm (16:57:47Z at c77d941, 2/2 in Chrome and Firefox), each exit 0; --platform linux in the WSL clone of 3662bb0 (17:17:05Z, clean tree): 2 selected, 2 passed, exit 0; 14 regressions at c77d941 exit 0. Still open: ordering criteria over labels (cdoc-jpha's collation); migration/ports/cfunc-m3.5.json's stale label statements (cfunc-m3.5 corrects them at its close).
