title: Prove the runner's wasm route runs real browsers
description:
## Outcome
`cargo xtask accept --platform wasm` records a case as passed in Chromium or Firefox only when that browser actually ran it, so cfunc-m0.1's wasm evidence is browser evidence and never a Node.js run.

## Context
Prerequisite of cfunc-m0.1, the first bead that declares wasm cases. Found by the infra-m0.3 refuters (2026-10-14): the wasm route sets only CARGO_TARGET_WASM32_UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN_RUNNER and CHROMEDRIVER or GECKODRIVER (tools/xtask/src/accept.rs:499-507); nothing forces a browser, and the outcome classifier never checks which browser ran (accept.rs:193-248). The excel and wasm not_run branches (Excel not registered, runner or driver missing; accept.rs:417-426, 464, 1016-1019) are exercised by no test. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask). Plan section 10.4: a wasm compile-only job is not browser validation.

## Do
Force browser execution for every wasm run and confirm from the runner's own output which browser executed each case; record that per browser in the receipt. Prove that `--list` and `--exact` select exactly one case under wasm-bindgen-test-runner. Add unit tests with an injected probe for each not_run branch (Excel absent, runner missing, driver missing). Install chromedriver matching the installed Chrome if the proof needs it, and name it in the commit message. Agents never run `--platform excel`.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform linux --require-all
```
- `dc_e8ql__browser_route` (registered under dc-e8ql in tools/xtask/acceptance.json, platforms windows and linux): a fixture wasm case that is not configured for a browser is recorded failed, never `<case>@chromium passed`; a fixture wasm case run in both browsers is recorded passed per browser with the browser's banner in its log; --list and --exact select exactly one case. On a host without the runner or drivers the case asserts the not_run outcome with its reason. Unit tests (`cargo test -p xtask --bins`) show each not_run branch with its reason.
## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution; the browser fixture runs on this Windows PC with Chrome and Firefox.

## Out of scope
CI (infra-m0.2); cfunc-m0.1's own cases.
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-14):
- Toolchain on this PC: Chrome 155.0.8059.40, Firefox 151.0.3, geckodriver 0.37.0 and wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.117 in %USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin. The orchestrator installed chromedriver 155.0.8059.39 there at claim, from Google's Chrome-for-Testing storage (the closest listed build of major version 155); the build commit names it. wasm-bindgen-test-runner requires the wasm-bindgen crate at exactly its own version, so the fixture pins wasm-bindgen =0.2.117 and a matching wasm-bindgen-test. The WSL Ubuntu clone has no browser, driver or runner. Node.js is installed on both Windows and WSL, so an unconfigured wasm test can run under Node and must not be scored as a browser pass.
- This bead gets its own case, dc_e8ql__browser_route, registered in tools/xtask/acceptance.json under id dc-e8ql with platforms windows and linux. It holds the browser scenarios, and its receipts are accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/<platform>.json, so infra-m0.3's committed receipts stay as its close cites them. Acceptance: `cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform windows --require-all` and `--platform linux --require-all`.
- The case builds a fixture package with one wasm case in a temporary workspace copy, then runs `accept --id <fixture bead> --platform wasm --require-all` through the real runner. On a host with both drivers it must show three things. (1) Each browser recorded passed only when the runner's own output names that browser: a forced-browser setting (for example WASM_BINDGEN_USE_BROWSER), plus a check of the banner wasm-bindgen-test-runner prints ("Running headless tests in Chrome/Firefox" or the like). (2) A fixture case that is not configured for a browser is never recorded `<case>@chromium passed`. (3) --list and --exact select exactly one case under the runner. On a host without drivers (the WSL clone) the same scenario asserts the missing-driver not_run outcome, with its reason. The receipt states which branch ran, so the Linux pass proves the not_run branch, and only the Windows pass proves real browsers.
- Unit tests inject the probes for every not_run branch: Excel not registered, runner missing, and each driver missing.
- Agents never run --platform excel.
close_reason:
Product status: the runner's wasm route forces browser execution (WASM_BINDGEN_USE_BROWSER=1, the other browser's driver variables removed) and records a browser's run as passed only under that browser's own runner banner; a 1-passed Node.js run is failed. Per-browser receipt entries record browser, banner, driver environment and executed_in (format dnacalc-accept-receipt/4). chromedriver 155.0.8059.39 installed for Chrome 155.0.8059.40. Build commit 6e904a2, pushed.
Evidence: Windows (rustc/cargo 1.94.1, chromedriver 155.0.8059.39, geckodriver 0.37.0, wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.117), accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/windows.json: "ACCEPT passed dc_e8ql__browser_route (package xtask, exit code 0)", RESULT passed, architecture checks 6/6, exit code 0; its notes record branch browsers: fixture_browser__alpha@chromium passed under "Running headless tests in Chrome" with user agent HeadlessChrome/155, @firefox passed under "Running headless tests in Firefox" with user agent Firefox/151, fixture_browser_node__alpha reported 1 passed under Node.js/25 and was recorded failed in both browsers, and the pre-change route had run the same fixture under Node.js and reported it passed. cargo test -p xtask --bins 62 passed (each not_run branch), fmt, clippy -D warnings, infra_m0_1__agent_contract 1 passed, infra-m0.3 Windows regression passed (its receipt restored unchanged). Linux (WSL Ubuntu, rustc/cargo 1.93.1, clone at 6e904a2), accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/linux.json: dc_e8ql__browser_route passed, RESULT passed, exit code 0, branch not_run (wasm-bindgen-test-runner not on PATH, so no real browser is proven on Linux; the driver-missing branch with a runner present is unit-tested only).
Still open: dc-pih5 (driver variables, banner position, versions in receipts, pinned fixture lock, driver-missing scenario with a runner present).

Format matters: calc-doc reads OOXML (.xlsx/.xlsm) only, so a .xls (BIFF) corpus needs each file converted by Excel (open, SaveAs .xlsx) before capture, which changes the file and adds a capture step.
1. Sheetpedia, xlsx edition: https://huggingface.co/datasets/tianzl66/Sheetpedia_xlsx (paper: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks, "Sheetpedia: A 300K-Spreadsheet Corpus"). Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (dataset card). 211,326 rows, 3.69 GB, .xlsx inside .tar.gz shards. Draws on Enron, FUSE and a crawl of Excel forums; already .xlsx, so no conversion. Adds: the largest formula-bearing set in OOXML, forum workbooks (formula-heavy, varied functions). Suggested first request: a sample of a few hundred to a few thousand files from one or two shards.
2. Enron spreadsheets (Hermans and Murphy-Hill 2015): https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.1221767 (figshare item "Enron Spreadsheets and Emails"). Licence: CC BY 4.0 (figshare metadata). spreadsheets.7z, 992,635,888 bytes (the emails are separate, 13 parts of about 734 MB, not needed). 15,770 spreadsheets, 9,120 with formulas; mostly .xls (BIFF), some in older formats. Adds: real business models (energy trading, finance), heavy on SUM/IF/VLOOKUP, dates and financial functions; needs .xls conversion.
3. VEnron (Dou et al., versioned Enron spreadsheets): 7,294 spreadsheets in 360 evolution groups, a subset of the Enron set; licence not found on the pages read. Adds: versions of one workbook, useful for edit and recalculation scenarios rather than function coverage. Would follow from item 2.
4. FUSE (Barik et al., MSR 2015): https://zenodo.org/record/581678. Licence: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo). fuse.zip, 9.4 GB, 249,376 spreadsheets extracted from Common Crawl, with JSON metadata (formula counts and functions per file), so a formula-dense subset can be chosen before download. Formats not stated (mostly .xls by the paper). Adds: breadth of web spreadsheets; needs .xls conversion for most.
5. EUSES (Fisher and Rothermel 2005): original at eusesconsortium.org (site linked from TU Graz); 4,498 spreadsheets from the web, mostly .xls; licence not stated on the pages read. TU Graz offers a modified EUSES (576 single-fault versions; cite Hofer et al. FASE 2013), licence not stated. Adds: a classic benchmark set; low formula density; licence needs confirmation with the source.
6. Apache POI test-data (spreadsheet folder): https://github.com/apache/poi/tree/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet. Licence: Apache 2.0 (the project). About 343 files, about 69% .xls and 24% .xlsx/.xlsm, including formula-evaluation fixtures (FormulaEvalTestData_Copy.xlsx, IndexFunctionTestCaseData.xls, IrrNpvTestCaseData.xls, LookupFunctionsTestCaseData.xls, countifExamples.xls, yearfracExamples.xls). Adds: edge cases chosen to test formula evaluation and file-format corners; small (tens of MB).
7. LibreOffice core spreadsheet test data: https://git.libreoffice.org/core/+/refs/heads/master/sc/qa/unit/data (also GitHub mirror). Licence: MPL 2.0 (the project). Many .xlsx/.xls/.ods files including per-category function tests (functions/ tests of statistical, text, database and other functions). Adds: function coverage with expected values written by another implementation's QA; .xlsx files usable directly, .ods not.
8. UK regulator and government models (Open Government Licence v3.0 where the site states it; ONS states OGL v3.0 for its dataset pages): Ofgem's other price-cap period models (Annex 9 levelised rates about 1.3 MB, pre-levelised rates about 5 MB per period) at https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/energy-policy-and-regulation/policy-and-regulatory-programmes/energy-price-cap-default-tariff-policy/energy-price-cap-default-tariff-levels; Ofwat PR24 financial and bill waterfall models (.xlsm) at https://www.ofwat.gov.uk/publication/pr24-bill-waterfall-model/ (licence not confirmed on the pages read: Ofwat's page refused the fetch); ONS datasets (mostly data, few formulas; .xls/.csv). Adds: large regulator models like the Ofgem one already in V1 (deep formula chains, financial functions), at a few to tens of workbooks.
Recommendation: request (a) the Apache POI and LibreOffice test-data folders (small, permissive, formula-focused), (b) a sample of Sheetpedia_xlsx shards (CC BY-SA 4.0, already .xlsx), and (c) the other Ofgem price-cap period models; Enron/FUSE after deciding on .xls conversion through Excel.

title: Lift reverse XLOOKUP values into the HSTACK spill in lookup-last-row-per-key
description: At c009674a, the committed lookup-last-row-per-key Excel 16.0.20527.20196 capture disagrees at Sheet1!N2. The static cargo xtask compare calculates one 3x2 spill, matching all three labels but giving #VALUE! in the second column where Excel gives 5, 11, 7. Formula is LET(keys,A1:A5,labels,UNIQUE(keys),HSTACK(labels,XLOOKUP(labels,keys,B1:B5,,,-1))). The evaluator records three XLOOKUP calls and one HSTACK. CalcFunc returns selected references; CalcFml retains references from lifted calls for their consumer. Isolate how XLOOKUP materializes results for an array of lookup values, preserving scalar reference behavior and existing reference-array consumers, before changing the shared lift. Use the existing hash-bound fixture/capture as the regression and workbook comparison. This is the newer HSTACK-labeled root from dc-ivym and the follow-up identified by dc-ebb.9.

title: CalcVBA: spec-driven conformance pass over MS-VBAL (clause index, Excel probe grids, coverage)
description:
Most of the language rules found by probing on 2026-11-16 are already written in MS-VBAL. Instead of finding rules one case at a time, run a conformance pass driven by the spec, with Excel as the oracle wherever VBE7 and the spec disagree.

Rules found by probing that the spec states:
- Let-coercion from an object gives its default member, Nothing raises 91, no default raises 438 (§5.5.1.2.13).
- Arithmetic, comparison, &, Like and the logical operators read an object operand's default member (§5.6.9.2).
- The logical operator type tables match LogProbe entry for entry.
- Omitted optionals get their declared default or the type default; Missing is a value of its own; errors 448/449/450.
- Bracketed foreign names (§3.3.5); VB_PredeclaredId and VB_GlobalNameSpace instances.

VBE7 behaviour the spec does not describe (Excel only):
- The class-object binary-operator rule (dc-kj6zf).
- Len(w) gives the default value.
- Nothing + 1 raises 13.
- w + Null raises 94.
- A Collection read with no index raises 450.
- Details the spec leaves to the implementation.

Source: CalcVBA docs/reference/microsoft-open-specs/MS-VBAL/[MS-VBAL]-250520.txt (9,800 lines; the formula pictures' alt text is in the .images.tsv beside it). MS-OAUT and MS-DTYP are in the same folder for the Variant and type rules. Do not use the Foundation pass07 extraction (garbled PDF text, keyword-picked items).

Steps, area by area (types and conversions, expressions and operators, statements, procedure invocation, then the §6 library):
1. Read the area's clauses and note each runtime rule and type table, with its line in the .txt. Keep this as a short list in the area's measurement folder, not a register.
2. Inspect the CalcVBA code that implements each rule (binder, OxIR elaboration, VM3, JIT helpers, runtime library) and check it does what the clause says, or what Excel does where they differ. Reading the code is evidence in its own right, not only the runs.
3. Probe what the code inspection or the clause leaves open: a COM-free grid measured once in Excel (scripts/run-inproc-probe.ps1, private desktop), kept under conformance/excel-measurements/<area>/, and run on VM3, the JIT and the typed host with the known-differences mechanism of crates/calcvba-differential/tests/object_operators_excel.rs.
4. Put each discrepancy, from the code or from a run, on one work list, and carry on checking. Do not fix during the checks.

When every area is checked, do the whole work list in one batch, then one check run afterwards. Keep it light: one pass per area, no extra registers or review rounds.

Done when every area has been checked against the code and probes, the work list is done or its remaining items are beads, and each area's list marks every rule as matching, a recorded difference from Excel, or not covered.
close_reason:
Done in CalcVBA d04b6f41 (probes, Excel answers, spec_pass_excel.rs) and 358375e7 (the fix batch).

- Inspection: every MS-VBAL area was checked against the code.
- Probes: 62 modules measured in Excel VBA. The differential test found 178 differing lines on VM3/JIT; 7 remain (conformance/excel-measurements/spec-pass/known-differences.txt).
- Leftovers:
  - dc-mtffw: call-site ByVal and positional-after-named refusals, plus corpus tests that encode them.
  - dc-jrthq: late-bound named ByRef, ParamArray Missing.
  - dc-bjt7v: Rate's last digits.
  - dc-qvc0f: MidB statement binding, InStrB compare.
  - dc-gs4bm: Windows checks (SpecStmt file cases, DLL rebuild and in-process re-run).
  - dc-pej5h: the ignored JIT reload host test.
  - strDate follows regional settings and is left to the locale work.

Every legacy node is a NodeView whose NodeId wraps a tree path (dnacalc-skin-ir/src/identity.rs); a skin that iterates node_order/children sits on the tree model, and the workbook profile never filled WorkspaceState.dependencies (stage-notebook S2.10).

Real and applicable to Excel workbooks (ported or to port):
- Tree (dnatreecalc-skins/src/tree.rs 964 + node_management.rs 688, 7 tests): foldable indented outline with subtree verbs. Excel form: workbook > sheet > used cells outline, folding by sheet, selecting a cell selects it in the session; the subtree verbs become the axis edits that exist. PORT as the tree skin.
- Flow (flow.rs 968, 4 tests): layered columns of chips, inputs left and results right, SVG wires, ]/[ grow the trace to dependents/precedents, off-trace chips dimmed. Excel form: a chip is a cell, a wire a precedent edge, the trace is Trace Precedents/Dependents. Needs a cell precedent/dependent read in calc-host (the engine's graph holds both). PORT as the canvas skin (the docs' Canvas skin itself exists only as HTML prototypes; Flow is the real canvas).
- Ledger (ledger.rs 1382, 12 tests): audit table (address, kind, content, value, provenance, format, dependency count) with filters (provenance, error, text, depends-on) and sorts. Excel form: a formula-cell audit table. PORT as the ledger skin.
- Lens/Console companions (companions.rs 318, spine_widgets.rs 866, 6 tests): selected-node inspector and health tallies. Excel form: the selected cell's detail (formula, value, format, precedents, dependents); taken into the canvas skin's side panel; the tallies already exist as the atlas.
- Workbook + grid_canvas, notebook, stage-sheet, stage-notebook, stage-atlas: already ported in dc-rif/dc-09v as the grid, notebook and atlas skins.

Real but left behind:
- Capture (capture.rs 1337, 19 tests): builds tree paths from typed segments (parse_path_segments, plan_scaffold); tree-reference language, no Excel form beyond the name box.
- FormulaTree (formula_tree.rs 294): a node navigator, not a formula parse tree; superseded by the tree skin.
- Bench (bench.rs 1748, 14 tests): scenarios on OxCalc's ScenarioProjection; no scenario support in the workbook engine.
- Sheet lens (sheet.rs 1634, 17 tests): value-first rows of tree nodes and Excel-table editing; the rows are tree nodes and calc-host has no table editing yet.
- Transport (transport.rs 1160, 12 tests): revision timeline on OxCalc's RevisionHistoryProjection; an Excel form (undo history list) needs an undo-stack read; not taken now.
- TripleEditor, OutlineTable, ValueBoard, DependencyInspector: the cell list + formula bar + value pane, the flat table and the value cards are covered by the notebook and ledger; the dependency inspector by the canvas skin's panel.
- Doc-only (no code): Canvas (constellation), Story, template-editor, format-editor, cell-view, nodes-across.

Skin IR: WorkspaceIntent (84 variants), SkinManifest/slots, versioned per-skin state, SharedSkinState, personas. DNA Calc keeps its own SkinId/Skin/SkinRegistry (dc-rif) and calc-host's SkinIntent; per-skin persisted state, slots and personas are not taken.

title: Linux-first Windows builds: cross-built binaries for daily work, native nightly validation
description:
Owner 2026-11-16 (not high priority; add to the work plans): regular DNA Calc development runs on Linux, with the Windows tests run on Windows from binaries cross-built on Linux (cargo xwin, docs/plan/WINDOWS_CROSS_BUILD.md). A daily native Windows build (night window 01:00-07:00) is the validation. Discrepancies between the cross-built and the native results are noted explicitly and kept in mind; they do not disqualify the mechanism, but each should be understood and resolved where possible. Long term: a reliable Linux build environment that produces the Windows releases.

State 2026-11-16: recipe works for debug builds (unit tests all pass, dna-calc-desktop 14/14 and dna-onecalc-desktop 21/21 integration tests, OneCalc page acceptance equal to native after dc-q2nd); not used since 2026-11-12 23:30 because the steps are manual.

Steps, in order:
1. One Linux command (cargo xtask) that cross-builds the Windows executables, test binaries, add-in fixtures and the web bundles, stages them and writes SHA256SUMS.
2. One Windows command that fetches a staged build into C:\Work\DnaCalc\xwin-builds\<UTC>, checks the hashes and runs the Windows tests and page acceptances from it (Excel and windows on a private desktop), with no cargo on Windows (replaces the CARGO metadata shim).
3. Test executables find their fixtures and companion binaries at run time (no compile-time Linux paths, no subst drive).
4. Daily native build in the night window: same tests from the native build, a short diff against the cross-built results of the same commit.
5. A discrepancy register in WINDOWS_CROSS_BUILD.md ("Known differences"): each difference, its cause when known, its status.
6. Release and perf profiles cross-built and compared.
7. Windows release artefacts (installers) produced from the Linux build; signing and publishing only with the owner's yes.

title: Report the calculation context HostState recalculates under
description:
## Outcome
calc_host reports the calculation context its recalculation applies (date system, iteration, precision as displayed), so a comparison derives the run's context fingerprint from the product, not from the capture or a constant.

## Context
Design of the real-workbook comparison (2026-10-21): calc-doc does not read calcPr, so HostState always recalculates in the 1900 date system, without iteration and at full precision. dc-qguw's round-2 judge note on infra-m1.3 asks that the record's context come from the run. ceng-m4.3 carries calcPr into the engine later and changes these values.

## Do
- A HostState accessor returning a plain struct (date1904, iteration, precision_as_displayed), with no enum variants nothing produces.
- Document that ceng-m4.3 changes the values; note on chost-m1.2.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
```
A generator-built package declaring date1904="1", iterate="1" and fullPrecision="0" opens through HostState::open and reports date1904=false, iteration=false and precision_as_displayed=false (what the host applies), and the case says which of them the package declared.

## Out of scope
Reading calcPr (ceng-m4.3).
notes:
Started 2026-10-21 by the DnaCalc session in the main clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc (br refuses the claim while chost-m1.1 is open; HostState is on master at 1de31fc). It is the first step of the owner's Excel comparison on real workbooks: dc-kt3l (`cargo xtask compare`) derives the run's context fingerprint from this accessor.
- The capability: a HostState accessor that reports the calculation context the host's recalculation applies (date1904, iteration, precision_as_displayed as bools, plus whatever calc_verdict's CalculationContext needs to build a fingerprint, such as the numeric mode the host was opened with), from the host's own state, not from the package; a separate accessor or field may report what the package declared (calcPr and date1904 from workbook.xml, as calc-doc loads them or does not), so a caller can tell 'declared' from 'applied'.
- Today the host applies the 1900 date system, no iteration and full precision whatever the package declares, because calc-doc does not read calcPr (ceng-m4.3 carries it into the engine later); document that and add no enum variants that nothing produces.
- Case: the bead's case name dc_hqcv__applied_context_reported, with a generator-built package declaring date1904="1", iterate="1" and fullPrecision="0": opened through HostState::open, it reports the applied context (false, false, false) and the declared one where the host can read it; a second package with calcPr absent reports the same applied values.
- Note on chost-m1.2 that its context item from infra-m1.2 lands here.

title: R4a: plans as plain data, plan verifier, schedule-perturbation harness
description:
R4a of the evaluator rework (dc-hsa5.20; REWORK_PLAN.md R4, 5.2 review C4 and C1).
Plans become plain data: Target holds a FunctionCallTarget<'static> pointer and calls() returns it (mod.rs:348); replace it by FunctionId plus a canonical byte encoding whose hash is the plan identity. Add a plan verifier: block and reference indexes, stack effects on every guard path, local/capture layouts, arity, one result per block, typed block/site ids. Drop RootSumFinalization from this package (both reviews agree).
Also here, first, the schedule-perturbation harness (5.2 C1, the idea left over from R1): a cargo xtask corpus mode that evaluates each workbook under (a) quantum 1 and unbounded, (b) an adversarial order (formulas offered reversed or shuffled, the UnscheduledRead check at recalc.rs:5884 turned into an ordinary wait for this mode), (c) 1 thread and N threads. Compare per cell: value bits, the evidence as sets, and the ordered effect sequence (user calls, draws, name-use records). Cross-cell order is excluded for (c) only (Excel varies there too, probe P08). Any cell whose outcome class changes under a perturbation is a finding before the later packages start. R1 pinned quantum per formula only, not on corpus workbooks (the engine exposes only 1024 and unbounded): expose quantum 1 to the harness.
Done when: the verifier runs on every plan of the corpus and the function bank with no fault; the plan identity hash is stable across runs; the harness report is committed with the per-cell comparison; corpus --oracle and witness judge --bank full are identical to before, debug and perf.

Model Excel's mechanism: one syntactic bit per formula (S), one always-calculate bit per cell, an ordered list of run-time events (CallDefault, Request), and one decision function always_calculate(profile, evidence) that replaces recalc.rs:2613-2619 and 5343-5346. The catalogue gets RecalcTrigger (DependencyOnly, Syntactic(cause), ByArgument(rule)). VolatilityEvidence (syntactic, last, builtin_ran_after_last, builtin_ran, events) joins the evaluation evidence. The three candidate rules F1 (sticky OR, today), F2 (one flag, attribute first) and F3 (set on execution) stay shadow-compared until the Excel probes decide; volatile() omitting Function targets is fixed by one fold. Calc-doc reads the file's ca attribute (load/sheet.rs:493): find or add the engine consumer so a by-request volatile cell loaded clean still recalculates on F9. Early cutoff never removes callbacks Excel would make in dependents.
Needs the volatility probes first (bead dc-hsa5.21: P1-P5 decide the layout).

title: R2: evaluation evidence as a replayable service tape with typed stop reasons
description:
R2 of the evaluator rework (dc-hsa5.20; REWORK_PLAN.md R2, 5.2 review C2): close the boundary with a service tape.
Define every outside interaction of an evaluation as a typed request and reply: area read, fact read, spill extent, binding probe, pending-producer answer (typed DependencyWait {cell, producer}), draw, clock, user call and its nested requests, RTD cut read. Area-level as today, never one record per cell. EvaluationEvidence returned with completion becomes a projection of the tape (reads as a set, effects as a sequence), not a second mechanism; evidence after a retried wait is a set by definition. Typed outcomes for quantum yield, dependency wait, host await and semantic re-evaluation (XLL provisional unwind) replace the single Suspended. Final dereference becomes a phase. Recording stays optional; correctness never depends on an observer.
Acceptance: any corpus evaluation re-run from its recorded tape, with no workbook present, gives the same bits and writes the same tape. That property is the conformance corpus for an evaluator in another language, the proof a worker needs only its inputs, the check for a compiled trace, and replay safety stated once. Use the R4a perturbation harness to show equal tapes across schedules.
Done when: tape replay passes on the whole corpus and the function bank, counts are identical, and the kernel conformance format (function id, argument bits, service replies, result bits) uses the existing function bank's rows, not a second corpus.

title: R3b: capability summary, restricted services view, evaluation-is-observable bit
description:
R3b of the evaluator rework (dc-hsa5.20; REWORK_PLAN.md R3, 5.2 review C3 and C10). Capability summary, restricted services view, and the "evaluation is observable" bit.
One conservative per-block/per-plan summary (structural and potential reads, facts, dynamic resolution, effects, recalculation policy, suspension/replay, result capabilities, explicit unknowns) from which the existing predicates (the 5.1 review lists fourteen consumers) are derived, shadow-compared with the old ones first. Declared capabilities are enforced: each kernel gets a services view restricted to what its catalogue entry declares (reads, facts, draws, clock, text binding, callables, volatility request); a use outside the declaration is a typed fault in debug and test builds. Run the function bank and corpus once: every fault is a wrong declaration found before any optimisation trusts it. This also removes the TextBinding built for every eager call (run.rs:1464-1468). A kernel declaring both draws and reads must retain progress across a wait.
Add one bit per plan, "evaluation is observable", distinct from volatility (smart recalc rule C10: the dirty cone spreads as in Excel; a pure node with representation-equal inputs may be skipped by certificate; a node with observable effects always runs).
Done when: every consumer reads the summary, the shadow report is empty, there are zero capability faults on the bank and corpus, and counts are identical.

title: R7: worker capability boundary
description:
R7 of the evaluator rework (dc-hsa5.20; REWORK_PLAN.md R7, 5.2 review C7 and section 5 items 5 and 7). Worker capability boundary: a checked worker view of services and concurrent callables, built inside the worker from immutable inputs. It needs the tape (R2) and the capabilities (R3b), not explicit frames, and it removes D5 (a dynamic prerequisite inside a concurrent scalar callback refused only in the parallel wave, so thread count changes an outcome class). Acceptance: Rc<dyn UserFunction>, the Rc<dyn Any> read view, Arc::ptr_eq closure identity and RefCell services are not reachable from the worker view (closure identity becomes a context-owned callable id). Only widening worker eligibility waits for probe P21.
Done when: the perturbation harness shows no outcome-class change between 1 and N threads, and counts are identical.

description:

title: R6: explicit frame machine, remove MAX_CALL_DEPTH
description:
R6 of the evaluator rework (dc-hsa5.20; REWORK_PLAN.md R6, 5.2 review C9). Explicit frame machine, the largest and riskiest package: a flat frame arena and one dispatcher covering blocks, lazy arguments, names, LAMBDA and kernel-to-LAMBDA helper callbacks; Excel's measured recursion budget is the only logical limit (removes MAX_CALL_DEPTH 64); nonrecursive teardown. First write down the kernel-to-LAMBDA callback protocol (the kernel returns a call request and is re-entered with the result): D2 showed the helper kernels are where recursion and suspension already disagree. Builds on dc-hsa5.18 (suspension without the per-call stack copy).
Done when: the measured budget is reached on the 1 MB wasm stack and MAX_CALL_DEPTH is deleted, not raised; counts are identical; the harness shows no outcome change.

title: R5b: call policy view and lifting stages
description:
R5b of the evaluator rework (dc-hsa5.20; REWORK_PLAN.md R5, 5.2 review C6). Call policy and lifting stages: a compiled CallPolicy view over the existing rules; lifting as explicit, independently testable stages; the "all scalar, no lifting" case split out (the prerequisite for batch execution later). The real work and the real parity risk: schedule it with the batch-execution evidence study (5.2 C8) and compare event sequences, not only values.
Done when: lifting stages are tested alone, counts are identical on corpus and bank, and event sequences are identical per cell.

title: R8: name code identity (shared immutable name bodies)
description:
R8 of the evaluator rework (dc-hsa5.20; REWORK_PLAN.md R7/R8 name part, 5.2 review P5 and section 5). Name code identity: shared immutable name bodies (NameBodyId) separate from per-use evaluation identity; volatility is a fact of the body joined at each executed use (what probe P5 decides); certified name-result reuse only later and only for eligible bodies. Relates to dc-hsa5.6 (name evaluation identities and views).

title: A clock RTD server: ticks for iterative models, as an engine test in Excel and DNA Calc
description: Owner 2026-11-12: instead of a push-based Tick (a self-referencing cell recalculated by hand), drive tick-based models from an RTD function, with control over start, pause, step, rate and reset. Shape: a small RTD server (COM, so Excel loads it too; DNA Calc through its RTD host route, dc-snz.23.4) with topics such as =RTD("DnaCalc.Clock",,"<model>","tick"), plus control topics or cells for run/pause, rate (ticks per second), step, and reset-at (a tick number or a condition cell). Each tick update triggers a recalculation in which self-referencing state cells advance once (iterative calculation, one iteration). Test cases: the Circular Reference workbook (lane game1) and the Names in Motion model (docs/fun/names-in-motion.html, the shop stock model). Evidence: the same sequence of ticks gives the same cell values in Excel and in DNA Calc, tick by tick, including a reset in the middle; also measures RTD throttling (Application.RTD.ThrottleInterval) and recalculation order with RTD. A second topic (a seeded random price feed) gives an event source at its own rate for discrete-event tests.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text: Owner 2026-11-12: the model must be evaluated by the calculation engine, not tweaked from COM or calculation events (those only for visualization), and the engine does no more than Excel. So the clock server only counts ticks and never reads the workbook: run and rate are RTD arguments, =RTD("DnaCalc.Clock",, model, "tick", Clock.Rate, Clock.Run), so changing those cells changes the topic through the formula; reset is a formula in the model (Clock.Reset = OR(Clock.Tick = Clock.ResetAt, <condition>)) that every state cell reads via IF(Clock.Reset, initial, ...). Step = a topic argument that changes (e.g. Clock.StepCount).

title: Shared formula UI library; DNA OneCalc stays engine-free
description: DNA OneCalc is a front end on CalcFml and CalcFunc only: formulas, formatting and (later) UDF integration without CalcEngine, CalcDoc or CalcHost. Today dna-calc depends on the dna-onecalc app for its formula field, display, result, theme and web start. Factor those into a shared UI library whose dependency ceiling is the same as OneCalc's (calc-fml, calc-func, calc-value, dna-strand; never calc-engine, calc-doc or calc-host); both apps depend on it and dna-calc no longer depends on dna-onecalc. Engine-backed UI (skin framework, controller, worker, wire, grid) stays in dna-calc. Make the ceilings mechanical in tools/xtask/architecture.json. UDF registration, when it comes (dc-snz), belongs at the calc-func/calc-fml level so OneCalc exercises it without the engine.

title: Evaluate IFERROR and IFNA lazily through calc_fml, ahead of LET and LAMBDA
description:
## Outcome
IFERROR and IFNA evaluate through calc_fml::evaluate and the catalogue: the value argument first, the fallback only when the value is an error (any error for IFERROR, #N/A for IFNA), with the array-context behaviour Excel documents.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison census (2026-10-21) finds IFERROR in the formulas of 19,648 cells of three real regulatory models, the largest single function blocker, and IFNA in 49. IFERROR sits in cfml-m2.4 (lazy control forms), which waits on cfml-m2.3 (LET and LAMBDA closures); IFERROR and IFNA need neither. IF already evaluates through the catalogue's BranchOnCondition demand (cfml-m1.3). This bead takes IFERROR and IFNA out of cfml-m2.4 (and IFNA out of cfunc-m3.21) so they land now.

## Do
- Catalogue entries for IFERROR and IFNA with a lazy argument demand, and calc-fml evaluation that evaluates the fallback only on an error; an error held in a reference or array argument follows Microsoft's pages.
- Cases with hand-derived values labelled documented or unmeasured, and the rows in an oracle workbook for an Excel capture; agents may run Excel on this machine (AGENTS.md), so capture it and compare.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform excel --require-all
```
IFERROR(1/0,5) is 5, IFERROR(2,1/0) is 2 without evaluating 1/0, IFNA(#N/A,1) is 1, IFNA(#DIV/0!,1) is #DIV/0!, and every row matches the Excel capture.

## Out of scope
IFS, SWITCH, CHOOSE (cfml-m2.4).
notes:
Claimed 2026-10-21 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-cfml. IFERROR is the single largest function blocker in the three Ofgem price-cap models the owner chose for the Excel comparison (19,648 formula cells call it).
- Port: look up every OxFunc and OxFml file you would read for IFERROR and IFNA (surface_dispatch.rs entries, their kernels and tests, OxFml's lazy-argument scheduling) with `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup`; port only exit 0 (exit 6 only against clean replacements); exit 5 or 3 is not read and the behaviour is written fresh from Microsoft's pages. Record each lookup and its exit in migration/ports/dc-ibp2.json.
- The capability to show, through calc_fml::evaluate (and calc_func's catalogue, which resolves the names):
  - IFERROR(value, value_if_error) and IFNA(value, value_if_na) evaluate value first and evaluate the fallback only when value is an error (any error for IFERROR, #N/A for IFNA); otherwise the fallback is never evaluated (show it: a fallback whose evaluation would be observed, for example through the ReadObserver or a refused call, is not reached).
  - An empty value is 0 as Excel's pages say (check what they say), and a value or fallback that is a reference is read as the pages say; an array or a range in an array context follows the pages or is refused with a typed not-modelled refusal (array lifting belongs to cfml-m3.4).
  - Reuse the lazy demand IF already uses (catalogue ArgumentDemand, calc-fml's branch evaluation) or extend it additively; do not add a second evaluation path.
- Cases: dc_ibp2__error_fallback (IFERROR and IFNA over values, errors of every kind, references to error cells and to cells holding values, nested inside arithmetic, and the not-evaluated fallback) with each row's expected value labelled documented or unmeasured choice, and an oracle workbook of these rows from a committed generator. Agents may run Excel on this machine (AGENTS.md, 'Excel on this machine'): capture that workbook with `cargo xtask capture` and add a comparison case that judges every row against the capture through calc_verdict, as cfunc-m1.2's comparison does, so the bead closes on measured agreement.
- Keep calc_fml's and calc_func's public signatures unchanged or extend them additively.
- What green does not show: IFS, SWITCH and CHOOSE (cfml-m2.4).

title: F2: port text, date and time, information, logical, lookup and database functions from OxFunc
description:
## Outcome
calc-func's catalogue holds OxFunc's text functions (including TEXT, VALUE, FIXED, DOLLAR with number formats), date and time functions, the rest of information (CELL and INFO through host facts), logical (IFS, SWITCH, LET-free remainder), lookup and reference (OFFSET, ADDRESS, INDIRECT's remaining forms) and database functions; web and cube functions refuse with a typed refusal.

## Do
- Port the modules wholesale, including locale_format.rs for number formats (en-ZA and en-US at least) and the date serial system (1900 and 1904).
- Known items to fold in: wildcard criteria over text beyond ASCII (was dc-o4do), digit text read as a logical (NOT("1")), text beyond the 404-character collation repertoire (was on cfml-m2.6), a number's text at a 16th-digit tie (was dc-rkzm), a direct blank in the SUM and COUNT family (was dc-uhdh), #BLOCKED!/#CONNECT!/#BUSY! over the IS functions and IFERROR (was dc-tt73).

## Port from
OxFunc crates/oxfunc_core/src (functions/, locale_format.rs, coercion*.rs, host_info.rs).

## Acceptance
Each commit builds the workspace and passes `cargo test` for the crates it touched, on Windows. The close note gives the corpus summary before and after (`cargo xtask corpus`, or `cargo xtask compare` on the Ofgem workbooks and the oracle workbooks until V1 lands), the package's test counts, and what is still refused, by area. One read-only review agent checks the honesty rules of AGENTS.md before the close.

## Plan
docs/plan/BULK_PORT_PLAN.md section 4.

Solving R'z = w by forward substitution fixes 8 of the 1-ulp cells and breaks 5 others (net +3), so it is not Excel's algorithm either; not adopted. The 10-observation set (rows 1094-1104, 2 to 10 ulp) and the 1-ulp cells need Excel's exact QR sequence.

title: Recorded rounding-family arithmetic: ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, TRUNC, MROUND digit counts and readings
description:
## Outcome
ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, TRUNC and MROUND return Excel's recorded bits on the OxFunc-Evidence scalar bank.

## Context
The 2026-11-04 problem table listed about 30,000 larger mismatches for ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, TRUNC, MROUND and MOD. Research found five structural rules:
- ROUND counts num_digits as a 32-bit integer: it keeps digits + e + 1 significant digits, with the sum wrapping in 32 bits.
- The directed functions read the low 16 bits of |num_digits|; out of range means 100 places.
- ROUNDUP adds its unit in binary64.
- 15-digit ties are read on the x87 unit at 64-bit precision when 10^|n| is exact (|n| <= 27).
- MROUND counts a quotient fraction within 5E-15 below a half up.

## Open after the first step
- 15-digit near-ties when the scale is above 10^27.
- ROUNDUP with tiny positive and negative inputs.
- DBL_MIN subnormal results.
- NaN bit patterns near DBL_MAX (needs a product decision).
- MOD with operands below 1e-290.

title: Excel NaN-bit numbers past DBL_MAX: downstream engine, display, TEXT and file behaviour
description:
## Outcome
A cell holding Excel's NaN bit pattern past DBL_MAX behaves downstream as it does in Excel, through the engine, display, TEXT and the file layer.

## Context
Owner decision, 2026-11-04: the calculation engine carries exactly the bits Excel produces. dc-j9k.18 makes ROUND, ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC return these numbers from calc-func, for example ROUND(1.7976931348623157E+308,-308) = 0x7ff1ccf385ebc8a0 (2E+308 with its exponent carried into the top field value). CalcValue::number keeps the bits, and `Site::number` already turns arithmetic on them into #NUM!. The rest below is not implemented.

## Measured (Excel 16.0.20527, Value2, A1 = ROUND(DBL_MAX,-308), A2 = ROUND(DBL_MAX,-307), A3 = ROUND(DBL_MAX,0), A4 = ROUND(-DBL_MAX,-308))
- Display: .Text is 2E+308, 1.8E+308, 1.8E+308, and 2E+308 for A4 (no minus sign).
- ISNUMBER TRUE, ISERROR FALSE, TYPE 1, ERROR.TYPE #N/A.
- =A1 keeps the bits, as do N(A1), MAX(A1), ABS(A1), IFERROR(A1,"err") and =-A1 (the sign does not change).
- =A1=A1 is TRUE and =A1>0 is TRUE.
- #NUM!: =A1+0, =A1*1, =A1-A1, ROUND(A1,0), SUM(A1), SUM(A1:A2).
- TEXT(A1,"0") is #VALUE!.
- Save: every such cell, and every cell that kept the bits, is written as t="e" <v>#NUM!</v>. ISNUMBER stays t="b" 1.
- Reopen: those cells read #NUM! until a full recalculation restores the bits.

## Do
Check each path against the list: comparison, unary minus, ABS, MAX and similar pass-through functions, general and TEXT formatting (`number_text::text` assumes a finite number and has a debug assertion), and the XLSX writer. Add the rows to an oracle section and capture them.

## Acceptance
Every row above matches through the product route, including save and reopen.

Evidence: nan-downstream.json and nan-downstream-sheet1.xml from the 2026-11-04 probe are in the dc-j9k.18 close note's evidence folder.

title: Identify GAMMALN, GAMMALN.PRECISE and GAMMA arithmetic
description:
## Outcome
GAMMALN, GAMMALN.PRECISE and GAMMA return Excel's exact binary64 results.

## Measured
Noise lines on windows of consecutive doubles (Excel 16.0.20527) separate the stored quantities of each band.
- GAMMALN, 3 < x < 8: z = (y+2)(y+3)..., left to right with every product stored; ln z stored; the stored [2,3] band value added and stored. 30,000 of 30,000 answers given GAMMALN(2+y).
- GAMMA, x < 10: (x-1)(x-2)...(1+y) from the top with every product stored, times the seed GAMMA(1+y), stored. 14,000 of 14,000 answers given GAMMA(1+y).
- GAMMA, x >= 10: sqrt(2 pi) x^x exp(-x) / sqrt(x) w, with binary powering of x and stored stages, in the code comment.

## Open
- GAMMALN on [0.7,1.5), [1.5,2) and [2,3]: rationals in x whose tables are not identified. The frozen steps of the mean residual locate where their Horner stages cross powers of two.
- The GAMMA seed on (1,2): a chain of stored products from binary64 sqrt(2 pi), about five stored smooth quantities; the Cody rational stands in for its value.
- GAMMA: Stirling series coefficients at x < 30, one further stored stage at x >= 30, x < 1 and negative arguments.

title: ODDFYIELD stops one Newton step short of the root
description:
ODDFYIELD returns a Newton iterate whose next step would be under 1e-10, not the root.

Measured (ld1, Excel 16.0.20527, question service): on 336 random odd-first bonds the price residual at Excel's yield is 1e-13 to 9e-8 and the residual over the price slope is below 1e-10 on every one (largest 9.85e-11), 321 below the root. A zero-coupon design shows bands of answers short by up to 8.9e-11: the stop is |step| < 1e-10 tested before the update. calc-func bisects to the root, so it misses nearly every call; the bank holds no ODDFYIELD rows and the corpus's 30 larger cells are one bond.

Open: the starting yield (not the rate, 0, 0.01 .. 1, YIELD on the same dates or one step from zero) and the slope (analytic or difference). Note: DnaCalc-Research design/odd-first-yield.txt.

title: BINOM.INV and CRITBINOM boundary rule over the public binomial tail
description:
BINOM.INV and CRITBINOM: smallest k with BINOM.DIST(0) > alpha at zero and BINOM.DIST(k, TRUE) >= alpha above it.

Measured (ld1, Excel 16.0.20527): 252 designed dyadic boundaries, each at the exact tail and three neighbours either side, all agree with that rule over Excel's own public tail. With calc-func's binomial tail the rule takes BINOM.INV 2,290 -> 2,302 of 2,308 and CRITBINOM 1,402 -> 1,414 of 1,420 but loses BINOM.INV(5,0.5,0.5) and its CRITBINOM twin, because calc-func's BINOM.DIST(2,5,0.5,TRUE) is 0.5 where Excel gives 0x3fdffffffffffffe; the six remaining misses are the same kind. So the patch (DnaCalc-Research evidence/ld1/binom-inv.patch) lands once BINOM.DIST matches those tails (round 46 owns BINOM.DIST). NEGBINOM.DIST: its 60 bank misses are all cumulative and Excel's NEGBINOM.DIST(f,s,p,TRUE) equals its BETA.DIST(p,s,f+1,TRUE) on 141/141, which calc-func already computes: the misses are the incomplete beta's. Note: DnaCalc-Research design/binomial-inverse.txt.

title: F.DIST and F.DIST.RT: how the beta argument pair is formed
description:

title: Identify ERF.PRECISE arithmetic beyond the generic libm approximation
description: ERF.PRECISE currently calls libm::erf. Correcting duplicated hex prefixes and a UTF-8 BOM in historical banks gives 251028 matched and 363313 failed of 614341 distinct recorded rows. The kernel itself is unchanged. Ordinary TOMS small-argument coefficient, series and square-root staging candidates lost previously matched rows and were rejected. Existing tiny rows contradict a single constant multiplication model. Identify the full arithmetic from recorded answers without answer lookups or fitting only the pinned sample.

The one-operation scalar model is impossible even with an unrounded constant: b16-g40-00002 requires K >= 1.1283791670955127013, while b16-g40-00007 requires K <= 1.1283791670955126696. Extended intermediate grids improved totals but lost matches: the tested 987 store mask gives 402682 full matches with 79989 losses, so was rejected. Cody numerator/denominator constant lattice search at +/-128 ULP also loses matches. All scratch candidates remain under target/witness/round2; none was ported into the product.

On the smaller |x|<2^-32 bank (131299 rows), sqrt-square followed by divide-sqrt-pi, Gamma(1/2)/pi and Cody numerator/denominator lattices also lose prior matches (best 100117, +54547/-15759). Split-linear forms from fdlibm/Boost-style high/low constants with native, stored and extended operations give best 100135, +54877/-16071; none retained. A bits 0x3ff1df5e70c7956b, B bits 0x3fefada15778ece6. These are coefficients inferred from recorded answers, not copied implementation coefficients. A one-billion-candidate reconnaissance on the short-significand grid isolated the numerator residue 0x156b modulo 2^15. The actual application-route full judge now confirms ERF.PRECISE 251028 to 385281/614341, 229060 remaining failures. title: bratio bup_160 near-DBL_MIN uncompensated exponent and -1.078e-14 offset (NEGBINOM.DIST/BETA.DIST s=933 f=1..5, 18 ww2 rows)
description:
Research the 18 ww2 Excel 16.0.20527.20196 discrepancies in bratio bup_160 near DBL_MIN (7..405 ULP): 15 NEGBINOM.DIST rows (s=933, f=1..5, p in {0x3fddc2cf0abec727, 0x3fdde6b1ea2e0cb4, 0x3fddf3d550cdb752}, where 933*ln(p) in {-714.384, -710.0, -708.4} < ln(DBL_MIN)) and 3 identical BETA.DIST(p, 933, 4, TRUE) rows.

Source files: ~/codex-runs/win-results/ww3/xl1/worksheet-intake/ww2/bank-rows/dc-iuwct.63-current-{NEGBINOM.DIST,BETA.DIST}.json.

Findings from dc-i2wk3 (xl2):
- Both Excel and CalcFunc evaluate p2 = 1 - q (confirmed at 714.384 where p != 1 - q) and retain the subnormal bpser term p^933.
- Current CalcFunc bratio_bup computes first * sum with compensated beta_density_at(a=1, b=933), giving a constant relative error across f=1..5, whereas Excel's relative error jumps by +-0.5 * 2^-43 (+-512 ULP) at every f=1..5.
- Forming the single right-associated binary64 exponent E = (s - 1)*ln(1 - q) + (ln(s) + ln((1 - q)*q) + ln(sb)) eliminates 100% of the +-400 ULP jitter across all 15 rows (whereas s*ln(1-q), left-associated sums, and first*sum all fail by +-400..+-900 ULP).
- Every one of the 15 rows then sits at a uniform residual ln(xl - p^933) - E in [-1.0847e-14, -1.0576e-14] (~ -48.6 * 2^-52, spread +-1..2 ULP) independent of f (1..5) and p.
- Meanwhile s=45000/181323 f=13 (x0 > 0.7, bup+bgrat) matches our first*sum path to -2..+1 ULP (5/8 exact), and s=933 f=0 (exp(933*ln(p))) matches 0 ULP.

Next measurements needed on Excel (Touchstone):
1. Probe NEGBINOM.DIST(f=1..5, s, p, TRUE) across varying s (e.g. s=200, 500, 933, 2000) and log(p^s) crossing -708.3964 (above and below DBL_MIN) to pinpoint the switch condition into the uncompensated exponent path.
2. Measure how the -1.078e-14 offset varies with s and x0 to identify its exact arithmetic source.

title: Witness bank design: tiers, when to retest, and archiving redundant ordinary rows
description: Owner 2026-11-21: the bank may grow too big (ISEVEN has 57,066 rows; ERF.PRECISE 618,437; 4,749,860 rows over 506 functions); think about how and when to retest and how/whether to archive entries. Proposal to settle: (1) tiers: pinned (about 120 rows a function, cheap, every lane check), active (per function: every edge class + every discrepancy ever seen + a fixed seeded sample of ordinary inputs), archive (everything else, kept in CalcFunc-Evidence, never deleted, replayable); (2) retest: a lane judges the functions it touches on the active tier; the whole active bank in the periodic sweep; the archive monthly or before a release; (3) pruning: only for functions exact on the full bank for a set time, never a row that ever differed, never an edge class (signed zeros, infinities and NaN payloads, subnormals, DBL_MAX, integers at 2^53, types: text, logical, error, empty, arrays, references); ordinary rows kept per class by a seeded sample sized by the function's numeric risk (more for last-bit functions, few for ISEVEN); (4) measure: judge run time per tier and bank bytes before -> after. Decision with the owner before any row leaves the active bank.

comments.author: koderbot
comments.text:
Commits d881b37c and 9ef49454 (Agent-Log dna-koderbot:claude/fix-1).

Root cause of the text-coercion group (189 of 276 jnt failures): the coercion routine already exists (coerce::number, then Site::read_text with the VALUE grammar of value_text.rs, which reads percent before or after, parentheses, spaces, signs, currency, grouping, exponents, dates and times). It runs only when the call has a locale profile, and the corpus harness takes the profile from the capture environment, which the function-question captures of jnt left null. The section captures now carry the environment of Excel 16.0.20527 on this machine (en-ZA, separators, a clock of 2026-11-09) via jnt_import.py environment; no answer is edited. One path still bypasses the profile: the dynamic-array reshape and LAMBDA helper count arguments (ported/dynamic_array_reshape_family.rs coerce_prepared_to_number) call coerce::number without a Site, so "50%" there is still refused; no row covers it.

Other fixes, each read from live Excel 20527: subnormal number literals that Excel accepts are 0 (=1E-308, =1E-309; =1E-310 cannot be entered) and the percent operator flushes a subnormal quotient; MID start bound 2147483648.9999995; 10^126 is 0x5A17A2ECC414A040 (PC64 double rounding), shared by POWER and PERMUTATIONA; HYPGEOM.DIST cumulative with a largest count of 0 is its one mass.

jnt workbook failing: 276 (82 mismatched, 194 refused) -> 79 (79, 0). Whole oracle corpus: pass 74853 -> 75050, fail 2104 -> 1907, no cell lost. Function bank (full, debug): 3887806 -> 3887817 of 3910795 rows, no function lost a row (PERMUTATIONA and POWER exact on every row).

Left: DATE 47 and POISSON.DIST 29 (research lane, untouched; the coercion work does not touch them). ROUND 2: the 15-digit reading of ties at shifts 168 and 313 follows x87 powers of ten that are not the nearest 64-bit constants; a single-constant model with the constant moved by whole units fits 301 of 561 probed shifts (28..321, -294..-28) against Excel, so the scaling is not one multiply or divide. HYPGEOM.DIST 1 (22 ulp, the open numeric class of the bank).

title: CalcVBA: late-bound named ByRef arguments and Missing for omitted ParamArray elements
description:
Two late-bound and ParamArray behaviours (spec-pass SpecExpr; Excel answers in SpecExpr.excel.txt):
- `lateNamedByRef`: a named argument in a late-bound call passes ByRef (Excel `o.Bump n:=lk` increments lk). Named arguments carry only a value through the IR (`CoreArg::Named`, `OxCallArg::Named`). Give them an optional ByRef place, lowered like `OxCallArg::ByRef`, and alias it in late dispatch in VM3 and rt-abi. The JIT also raises an error with number 0 on this call today.
- `paOmitted`: an omitted ParamArray element is Missing (VarType 10, IsMissing True). CoreIR and OxIR have no Missing constant, and natives receive omitted arguments as Empty. Add `CoreConst::Missing`/`OxConst::Missing`, materialised as the DISP_E_PARAMNOTFOUND error value in VM3 and the JIT, and use it in `paramarray_element`.

Done: both lines leave spec-pass known-differences.txt on VM3 and the JIT.

title: CalcVBA: VBE7 binary-operator rule for a VBA class object held in a Variant (w + 1 is 42)
description:
VBE7 answers a binary operator over a VBA class object held in a Variant with that object's default member, dropping the operation, which MS-VBAL does not describe (its operators are simple data operators). CalcVBA does the spec's normal operation. Measured in Excel 16.0 build 20527 (probes temp/variant-layout-probe/ops13, Ops2Probe/Ops3Probe; kept COM-free in conformance/excel-measurements/object-operators with the open lines in known-differences.txt; w and s are Variants holding VBA class objects with defaults 42 and 7, o As Object, d As a class type, MakeV() a function returning a Variant object).

Rule found (both operand orders, all of + - * / \ Mod ^ & Like And Or Xor Eqv Imp; comparisons and unary operators are not affected; COM objects such as a Range are not affected):
1. If the right operand is not a call result and holds a VBA class object, the answer is the right operand's default (w + s = 7, s + w = 42, 1 + w = 42, w + a(1) = 7, w + (s) = 7, w + CVar(s) = 7, r + s = 7).
2. Else if the left operand holds a VBA class object and the right operand is not a call result, the answer is the left's default (w + 1 = 42, w & "x" = 42, MakeV() + 1 = 7, s + r = 7); a Null right operand raises 94.
3. Else (the right operand is a call result: MakeV(), a static Object/class operand converted by a default get, (o)) the operation is ordinary (w + MakeV() = 49, w + o = 84, MakeV() + MakeV() = 14).
"Call result" = a procedure, member or default-member call; variables, elements, fields, parentheses, constants and library intrinsics (CVar, Abs, CInt) are not.

Implementation note (2026-11-16 attempt reverted): an elaboration-time expansion (a native picking the operand, IsObject, a late default get) worked on VM3 and the JIT but the typed host could not admit it and it added two calls to most Variant operations. Do it inside the operators instead (VM3 Arith/Div/Pow/Concat/Logical and the Like native; the JIT's Variant helpers), where the object check is free for non-objects, with one bit from elaboration per operator site: whether the right operand is a call result (an OxIR field on Arith/Div/Pow/Concat/Logical, about 130 sites, or an equivalent). Done when known-differences.txt is empty and the probes match on VM3, the JIT and the typed host.

title: Compare a workbook's DNA Calc calculation with its Excel capture, cell by cell, and classify every difference
description:
## Outcome
`cargo xtask compare --fixture <xlsx> --capture <capture.json> --out <dir> [--exact-target ...]` opens a real workbook through calc_host (HostState::open, step with an unlimited budget, project), judges every formula cell of the capture's inventory with calc_verdict::judge against an evaluation record built from the evaluator's own reports, and writes report.json, evaluations.json and triage.json, with a one-screen summary: inventory, calculated, matched, mismatched by class, not modelled by root key with the cells each root blocks.

## Context
The owner (2026-10-21): compare DNA Calc with Windows Excel on real workbooks on this machine to guide development, correctness first, then performance. The Excel capture adapter (infra-m1.2) records every formula cell of a workbook after a full rebuild; nothing on the DNA side yet evaluates a whole workbook into a result set. This bead is the only product writer of the evaluation record (infra-m1.3 builds on it; one verdict feed, AGENTS.md).

## Do
1. Refuse unless sha256 of the bytes equals the capture's source.
2. HostState::open; on OpenFailure every inventory cell is missing with the typed error.
3. step with a ReadObserver recording evaluated reports, calls and read areas; drop all evaluations when step fails.
4. Project exactly the inventory cells; map ProjectedValue onto calc-verdict's Provenance (Calculated with the context from the context-report bead, FileCached, Stale, NotModeled with its typed refusal, Empty or Literal as missing).
5. Judge in-process; write the report and the InstrumentRecord.
6. Triage: each inventory cell gets exactly one class (capture, doc, engine, context, formula, function-missing, kernel-value or kernel-bits, matched) and a key (the typed refusal, the function spelling, the LoadError variant), with root cells and cells blocked only because they read a root kept apart. A difference in a calc-func kernel's result is classed kernel-value or kernel-bits with the FunctionId, the argument values the reads show, both results' bits, the ulp distance and agreement to 15 significant digits.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform excel --require-all
```
<bead>__every_cell_classified (windows): a generator-built workbook and a capture authored in the test with hand-derived Excel values (labelled as such) holding a SUM chain, a deliberately wrong formula cache, a not-modelled function and a reader of it: every inventory cell gets one class, and the wrong cache never scores. <bead>__live_capture (excel): the same workbook captured live on this machine and compared.

## Out of scope
Fixing what the triage finds (the Ofgem comparison bead files it).

title: Let the context fingerprint ignore iteration limits while iteration is off
description:
## Outcome
calc_verdict's context fingerprint depends on the iteration limits only while iteration is on, and a caller can build a context without iteration limits, so a run whose host applies no iteration derives the whole fingerprint from its own context.

## Context
dc-hqcv's round-1 judge (2026-10-21): CalculationContext::fingerprint (tools/calc-verdict/src/session.rs) always formats max_iterations and max_change, which HostState's applied context cannot supply (the host applies no iteration), so `cargo xtask compare` (dc-kt3l) would have to take them from the capture or a constant. With iteration off the limits change no value; the capture worker forces 100 and 0.001 then.

## Do
- With iteration off, fingerprint() names Excel's default limits (100 and 0.001) whatever the context holds, so captures taken with iteration off keep their fingerprint.
- CalculationContext::without_iteration(date1904, precision_as_displayed).
- A unit test: two contexts with iteration off and different limits have one fingerprint; with iteration on they differ.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform windows --require-all
```
The unit test passes, and every existing capture and evaluation fixture keeps its fingerprint.

## Out of scope
Iterative calculation (ceng-m5.2).
close_reason: Built in d6cc2c2 (calc-verdict): CalculationContext::fingerprint names Excel default iteration limits (100, 0.001) while iteration is off, and CalculationContext::without_iteration(date1904, precision_as_displayed) builds such a context. capture_v2_tests::the_calculation_context_fingerprint_names_every_setting shows the string for iteration off with the defaults is unchanged, three other limit pairs leave it unchanged while iteration is off and change it while iteration is on. Windows: cargo test -p calc-verdict --lib 40 passed; infra-m1.1 windows and wasm and dc-qguw windows passed. Linux in WSL at 4922f25: calc-verdict lib 40 passed, infra-m1.1 and dc-qguw linux passed. A read-only reviewer checked every producer and consumer of the string before the push. dc-hqcv adds the first non-test caller.

title: Derive infra-m0.5's tainted-commit list by rule, check it at accept time, and review ffcb9a77
description:
## Outcome
migration/numeric-provenance.json's tainted_commits list is derived from a rule the record states, the infra-m0.5 case recomputes it from `git log` at the pinned commit and fails when a commit is missing, and an independent reviewer's verdict on OxFunc commit ffcb9a77 is recorded by that reviewer, so infra-m0.5 can close.

## Context
Prerequisite of infra-m0.5, holding its close (2026-10-15). infra-m0.5's round-3 judge left two blocking findings after the third implementer round: (1) the tainted-commit list was hand-picked (16 commits) while the record's own reasons name a class (W108/W109 identification commits) that `git log -i -E --grep='W10[89].*identif|identif.*(graph|staging)|IDENTIFIED' 6fca3518` finds 64 of, and the case only checks that five named commits are present (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_5.rs:1216-1235); (2) the implementer alone decided not to list ffcb9a77, which modified excel_numeric/x87.rs and mod.rs and added smart-fuzzer/tools/w111/complex_kernel_probe (a tainted class) as well as the W111 captures. As a conservative data fix the orchestrator listed every commit matching the stated rule (identification commits, and every commit whose message holds one of the record's 15 sweep patterns: 70 commits) plus ffcb9a77, pending this bead. Infrastructure files only. The infra-m0.5 reading rule applies.

## Do
State the derivation rule in the record and make `cargo xtask pin-sources` and the accept-time check derive the list from git at the pin, failing on any omission; run an independent review (a separate reviewer agent, its verbatim output committed) of ffcb9a77 and of every commit the rule adds, with witness independence argued from the capture files' own acquisition, not from a commit being unlisted; apply the verdicts; remove from both migration files the remaining staging residue (the 87disp control-word value and the helper instruction sequences quoted at numeric-provenance.json:76, 130-141, 163, 343-344, and the staging tokens listed in infra_m0_5.rs:68, 1814), keeping only citing clauses; settle the disposition of extended-numeric/numeric-outcomes.json and check, rather than assert, that it was written before the freeze steps.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.5 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.5 --platform linux --require-all
```
A fixture in which the record omits a commit the rule finds makes infra_m0_5__quarantine_gate fail; `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` exits 5 for OxFunc functions/combin.rs, combina.rs, matrix_family.rs, misc_conversion_family.rs, regression_forecast_family.rs, beta_gamma_stats_family.rs, chi_f_t_family.rs, statistical_tests_family.rs, asin.rs, acot.rs and atan.rs unless a reviewed per-file entry clears one; the review file holds the reviewer's ffcb9a77 verdict.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Clearing any catalogue file (dc-2203).
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-15):
- Order: an independent review first, then the implementer round. The review is a separate, read-only reviewer agent whose verbatim structured output is committed as migration/numeric-provenance-review-2026-10-15-commits.json. It gives a verdict on ffcb9a77 and on each of the 55 commits the stated rule added. For every file the witness chain depends on, it says whether that file's own acquisition evidence shows black-box Excel capture independent of the tainted research that ffcb9a77 also carries: the five answer captures, extended-numeric/numeric-outcomes.json and its writer retain_numeric_campaign.py, the runner Run-W109BulkBatch.ps1 at the blob that ran, CellRefBatch.psm1, run_numeric_campaign.py, the input generator, and the snapshot and freeze scripts. It also checks the ordering claim, that the retention was written before the freeze steps.
- Precedence change: a file changed by a listed tainted commit stays at least unresolved unless a reviewed per-file entry clears it and names that commit as considered. The witness chain is admitted only through such entries.
- The tainted-commit list is derived by the stated rule (W108/W109 identification commits, plus commits whose message holds a sweep pattern), plus the commits the review ties to the pass. Both `cargo xtask pin-sources` and the accept-time check recompute it from `git log` at the pin and fail on any omission.- Review done (2026-10-15, workflow run wf_5ba77a06-ea9; saved verbatim as migration/numeric-provenance-review-2026-10-15-commits.json). The 55 rule-added commits: 22 tainted, 24 unresolved, 9 not_tied_to_pass. ffcb9a77: tainted. All 15 witness-chain files are cleared on their own acquisition evidence, or as having supplied no bits. Retention-before-freeze: not established, so witness independence rests on hash continuity. The reviewer reported reading_rule_kept=false and disclosed incidental reads of script code beyond docstrings; it read no x87 body.
Rulings after round 1 (2026-10-15, orchestrator): (a) Names used as labels in a citing clause are citations, not staging, and may stay: an instruction mnemonic such as F2XM1 or FYL2X, a chain label such as fFEXP, or a symbol name such as excel_x87_mul. What must not appear is a staging formula, an instruction sequence, a control-word value or a code line. The verbatim commits review stays as written. (b) Four witness-independence limits are owned by dc-z5ay (its notes now name them). (c) The work done here is recorded on dc-qfqa and dc-2203.
Rulings after round 2 (2026-10-15, orchestrator): (a) The infra-m0.4 Windows regression compares against HEAD's committed manifest, so the orchestrator runs it after the build commit; infra-m0.4's Linux run on the pushed commit, with its committed receipt, also comes with this bead's close. (b) Round 3 limits the acquisition lifting of the tainted-commit rule to files that supply expected bits (the five answer captures and the retention). Scripts the review cleared only for their witness-chain role keep the provenance the content rules give them for porting, so their `--lookup` must not read as clean port inputs. (c) Code-line quotes are not allowed even when they carry no staging content (ruling (a) of round 1). The gen_tables.py PROBE path assignment and the excel_bond_pow signature line become citing clauses. (d) The remaining round-2 follow-ups belong to dc-qfqa (its notes list them), and dc-1c6a now depends on dc-qfqa.
Ruling after round 3 (2026-10-15, orchestrator): Cargo.toml lines that name features only, for example features = ["research-x87"], are configuration quotes and may stay. Ruling (c) applies to code that could carry derived content. The round-3 follow-ups are recorded on dc-qfqa.

An independent reviewer (workflow run wf_5ba77a06-ea9) recorded verdicts on the 55 rule-added commits, ffcb9a77 and 15 witness-chain files (migration/numeric-provenance-review-2026-10-15-commits.json). title: Excel service: one crashing GAMMA.DIST batch took all three workers down for 57 min
description:
2026-11-15 04:17:40Z: a fix4 request (04ee1000, GAMMA.DIST, 512 calls; probably the subnormal boundary controls of dc-ymjf.2.141) crashed Excel on w2, and the same calls merged into a POISSON.DIST+GAMMA.DIST batch crashed w1. The broker retried the calls; within 42 s w1 and w2 each crashed three more times, w3 too, and at 04:20Z all three workers hit the restart cap (3 per 60 min). No worker answered from 04:20Z to 05:17:40Z (57 min); fix4 worked on without Excel answers. Evidence: codex-runs/excel-service-v2/log/waits.jsonl and log/2026-11-15.jsonl.gz (batches 57819-57820 onwards); GAMMA.DIST is now in isolated.json.

Wanted:
1. After a crash, do not retry the crashing batch on the healthy workers; split it on the isolation worker only (bisect to the crashing call), and keep the other workers serving other functions.
2. The restart cap must never leave every worker down: crashes caused by isolated or bisected calls should not count against the shared workers, and at least one worker stays up for non-isolated functions.
3. Return the bisected crashing call(s) to the caller as a typed result (excel-crashed with the arguments), so the lane gets the crash as an answer instead of a wait; record them in a crash list for the handbook (Excel crashing on an input is itself a recorded behaviour).
Done when: a test with a fake worker that crashes on one marked call shows the other calls answered, the marked call returned as excel-crashed, and no worker hits the cap.

title: Rule on the dna-koderbot deployment and test-machine plan (owner)
description:
## Outcome
The owner has ruled on each decision of the dna-koderbot deployment and test-machine plan, so that its beads can be sharpened and claimed.

## Context
The planning workflow wf_74ca3b42-eea (2026-10-18: read-only surveys of the repository and of dna-koderbot, three independent proposals, a synthesis, security and process critics, and a revision) produced the plan in dc-gh6q. Every bead of that plan depends on this one. It stays deferred, so that br ready never offers the plan's beads before the owner has ruled. The orchestrator closes it on the owner's word and records each ruling here.

## Do
Record the owner's ruling on each decision:
- Hostnames: decided by the owner on 2026-10-18. DNA Calc is served at the apex dnacalc.com, and DNA OneCalc at onecalc.dnacalc.com. The apex serves the home release until DNA Calc's first publish (C2).
- Retirement. Apex and www, dnatreecalc, and dnaonecalc are each approved separately. dnaonecalc either redirects to the apex at the cutover or keeps the preview until O2 (the flag in expect.json). Also decide how long to keep the backups and the old DNS records.
- Host access (K1a), required before K1b and S2:
- remove or touch-protect the agents' koderbot key;
- remove koderbot's NOPASSWD sudo and lxd membership;
- use ubuntu as a touch-required admin user.
This also cuts other projects' agent access through the koderbot alias, and any koderbot automation that relies on sudo needs checking.
- Agent credential. A fine-grained token without Workflows permission, with the owner pushing every workflow commit. Cost: the agent's clone stops until each push (dc-b7w4, K1b, K2, K3, K4, S2). The org must allow fine-grained tokens. Also turn on org 2FA.
- AGENTS.md amendments (K1a, K2, K3): the held category for owner steps, workflow pushes by the owner, no ssh route to dna-koderbot, the runner workspace as a full clone, the koderbot trust level, koderbot as a Linux evidence source, and the triage rule. Also decide whether work prompt Â§3.5 changes to match.
- Container limits (8 CPU, 24 GiB, 140/150 GiB disk), the egress ACL and the firewall rules. If you decline the ACL, K1b's network expectations must change.
- Legacy root on dna-koderbot (K4), carried in by bundles made on your PC. The alternative is to keep infra-m0.4 and infra-m0.5 on WSL.
- GitHub Free: artifact retention for ci.yml as well (Free includes 500 MB of storage; 51.9 MiB is used after 4 days). A CI publish route (old S4) needs a plan with required reviewers on private repositories; until then it is not filed, and publishing stays owner-run.
- Graph: whether onecalc-m8.1 and dnacalc-m8.1 should depend on O2 and C2. Notes naming `site bundle` are added either way.
- Public /build.json fields: site, commit, built UTC and file hashes. This exposes private commit SHAs. Receipts stay in published.json, inside the private repository.
- Browsers in the container: not filed.
- Tracker status page: not filed.
- HSTS (one year, without preload) only after a clean cutover.
- Standing approval: not available for any route yet.
- Hardening:
- move Caddy admin to a unix socket;
- check cups on 631;
- keep the LXD API off the network;
- review the unauthenticated proxied service.
- Priorities. Proposed:
- P1: W1, K1a, K1b, K2, K3, K4, R1, S1, S2;
- P2: S3, O1, O2;
- P3: C1, C2.
None blocks M1.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
br show <this bead>
```
Each decision above has a recorded ruling.

## Platforms
None (owner decisions).

## Out of scope
Implementing any bead of the plan.

title: CalcVBA: conversions and operators on a Variant-held object take its default member (incl. VBA's binary-operator oddity)
description:
Conversions and operators on an object held in a Variant do not take its default member in CalcVBA (both backends), unlike VBA. Measured in Excel (probes temp/variant-layout-probe/let12, LetProbe and OpProbe; class Dflt whose default member returns 42; w As Variant holding a Dflt, o As Object holding it):
- ByVal argument to a Long parameter `LongArg(w)`: VBA 42; CalcVBA error 13.
- `CStr(w)`: VBA "42"; CalcVBA error 13. `CLng(w)`: VBA 42.
- `w = 42`: VBA True; CalcVBA False.
- VBA oddity to copy bit for bit: a binary operator with a Variant-held object operand gives the object's default value and drops the operation. `w + 1`, `1 + w`, `w * 2` and `w + w` are Integer 42; `w & "x"` is Integer 42. With `o As Object`, `o + 1` is 43. Unary `-w` is -42; `CDbl(w) + 1` is 43. CalcVBA gives 43 for `w + 1` today.
Work: shape first. Probe more operators (comparison operators other than =, Mod, \, ^, Like, And/Or, Is) and both operand orders, Variant vs Object static types, and a project object vs a COM object (Range). Then implement once for VM3 and the JIT, reusing CoreValue::LetValue where a conversion takes the default member.
close_reason: CalcVBA b261c4d93: operators (compare, &, Like, logical, Not, conditions), conversions and library functions read an object default member as MS-VBAL simple data values and Excel do; typed ByVal params; Nothing 13 in arithmetic and 91 in conversions; logical result types per the spec table (150 library-tranche and 11 numeric-mode-matrix differences fixed). Excel probes match on VM3 and the JIT except the VBE7 class-object operator rule (new bead) and JIT declines on Abs(Variant) and Not of float constants (new bead).

title: independent_lanes: leave cargo's last-use tracker out of the shared cargo-home check
description:
## Outcome
infra_m0_1__independent_lanes passes or fails on what the four lane builds do, not on cargo's own bookkeeping: an update of cargo's last-use tracker in the shared cargo home is not reported as a lane writing shared state.

## Context
2026-10-21, on master 60c338d with a clean tree: `cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all` failed once with 'the lane builds changed the shared cargo home C:\Users\GovertvanDrimmelen\.cargo: [".global-cache"]' (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance.rs, the case's cargo-home comparison), and passed on the next run of the same commit. .global-cache is the SQLite database in which cargo records when each cached registry crate was last used; cargo refreshes those times only when they are older than its update interval, so whether a build writes it depends on when the crates were last used, not on the lane's behaviour. Other cargo processes on the machine (lane clones building at the same time) can also write it.

## Do
- Leave .global-cache (and its -wal/-shm companions, if present) out of the cargo-home comparison, and say why in the case's evidence; or show that a lane's own build wrote it and report that separately from a lane writing anything else.
- Keep every other path of the cargo home compared.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all
```
A probe that touches .global-cache during the lane builds leaves the case green with an evidence line naming it; a probe that writes any other file under the cargo home turns it red.

## Out of scope
Changing cargo's own garbage-collection settings.
close_reason: Build 328d822 and receipt b05a3a0: infra_m0_1__independent_lanes leaves cargo's last-use tracker out of the cargo-home comparison; infra-m0.1 passed on the committed tree with infra-m0.2..m0.6, dc-e8ql, dc-cyd7 and dc-kt3l passing on windows.

title: CalcVBA library: named arguments to library functions do not bind (93 cases, masks 78 modules)
description:
Named arguments to VBA library functions mostly fail to bind. Example: `Left(String:="abc", Length:=2)` gives "unresolved name `String` (named argument)".
- **Scale:** 93 probe cases, and a failing case stops its whole module binding, which masked results in 78 modules. (vba_library_excel.rs then re-runs each case alone, which is slow; the executor tests are #[ignore]d until this is fixed.)

- **Excel refuses some forms** (`compile-refusals.tsv`), and CalcVBA must refuse them too:
  - named arguments to Abs, Fix, Int, Sgn, InStr, InStrB and StrComp: "Syntax error";
  - `InStr(1, "abc", "b", Compare:=...)`: "Object doesn't support named arguments";
  - CallByName's ParamArray: "Argument in ParamArray may not be named".

Done: every named-argument case in the probes matches Excel, and the refusals stay refused.
