title: CalcVBA math: Sin (and likely other transcendentals) last bit differs between Linux and Windows; use one Excel-exact implementation
description:
Sin's last bit depends on the host platform. CalcVBA calls the platform libm (Rust f64::sin), so results differ between Linux (glibc) and Windows (MSVC CRT).
- **The case:** library_tranche_excel Sin.6 and Sin.8. Excel gives 0.598472144103957; on Windows CalcVBA gives 0.598472144103956 (VM3 and JIT); on Linux it matches.
- **Likely scope:** the other transcendental functions (Cos, Tan, Atn, Exp, Log, Sqr is exact) probably behave the same way. The vba-library probes' lastbit lines were measured on Linux only.

Bit-exact is the only accepted state, and it must not depend on the host. Implement the math functions with platform-independent code that reproduces Excel VBA's results (VBE7 uses the MSVC x64 CRT), shape first as in the CalcFunc bit-exact programme.

Done: library_tranche_excel and the vba-library Math probes match on Linux and Windows alike.

  - MatchCollection and SubMatches: Item, Count, _NewEnum.
- **Semantics:** the VBScript regular expression dialect (as in VBScript_RegExp_55). Its error numbers for bad patterns are in the probe answers.

title: CalcVBA library: date and number text ignores the host regional settings (250 locale cases)
description:
Text that depends on the regional settings differs from Excel. CalcVBA formats and parses date and number text with fixed US conventions (m/d/yyyy, 12-hour AM/PM). Excel follows the host's regional settings; the measuring machine uses South African settings: yyyy/mm/dd, 24-hour time, period decimal separator.
- **Scale:** 250 probe cases marked `' locale`.
- **Functions affected:** CStr and the implicit conversions of Date; CDate, DateValue and IsDate parsing of date strings; Format named formats (General Date, Short Date, Long Time…); FormatNumber, FormatCurrency, FormatPercent and FormatDateTime; Str of dates.

This needs a locale model, not per-function fixes: the host's LCID with its date order, separators and time format; for a desktop host, the user's regional settings.
- The in-process Excel host has the same values Excel uses, and the probes give the en-ZA answers.
- Choose how a non-Windows host picks a locale.
- The locale work (en-ZA agreement, locale switching) is on the DNA Calc side as well; share the model.

Done: the locale cases match Excel's en-ZA answers under an en-ZA locale. A second locale (for example en-US, measured by switching the test machine's settings) also matches.

title: Give a number's text as Excel gives it when & or a function reads the number as text
description:
## Outcome
calc_func gives a number's text as Excel gives it when an operator or a function reads the number as text (the & operator first), so formulas such as A1&"-"&B1 or "="&D$145 over a number compute instead of being refused as not modelled.

## Context
The Ofgem comparison (dc-3t1b): 1,402 cells of the three price-cap workbooks use &, and refuter 2 of cfunc-m3.5 counted 1,472 criteria in Annex-4 built as "op"&cell over a number. crates/calc-func/src/coerce.rs `text` refuses every number (owner GENERAL_TEXT, cfml-m2.6). cfml-m2.6 is the whole number-format service (TEXT, cell display, locales); this bead takes only the conversion a number gets when it is read as text, in en-US, with no column width. cfml-m2.6's service later takes it over unchanged.

## Do
- Implement the conversion in calc-func's coerce module (the only site today) for every finite binary64: up to 15 significant digits, the switch to E notation and its exact form (E+15, E-07, mantissa digits), negative numbers and negative zero, as Excel gives them. Port from OxFunc where `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` exits 0 for the file read; otherwise write it from measurement.
- Measure the rows in Excel on this machine (agents may run Excel; see AGENTS.md): an oracle workbook from the committed generator, its rows compared through calc_verdict once `cargo xtask capture` works; until then the comparison case is not_run with MissingCapture and every row's expected text is labelled with how it was obtained.
- Narrow the GENERAL_TEXT owner in calc-func's acceptance tables to what still refuses; note on cfml-m2.6.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform wasm --require-all
```
Rows through calc_func::invoke of & with a number: integers up to and past 15 digits, the boundaries around 1E+15 and 1E+21, small numbers from 1E-4 to 1E-10, sums whose 16th and 17th digits differ from their 15-digit text (0.1+0.2, 1/3, 2/3, 1-1E-16), negative numbers, negative zero, the largest and smallest normal and subnormal doubles; each row's text equals Excel's.

## Out of scope
TEXT and number formats other than this conversion, cell display, locales other than en-US (cfml-m2.6).
close_reason: Built in 515af81 (text lane, four rounds; the round-4 judge allowed the close; the orchestrator wrote the tracker items in 7cb8f96 and corrected four wording points, and a read-only reviewer checked them and the message). calc_func::invoke of & gives Excel's text when it reads a number as text (crates/calc-func/src/number_text.rs, through coerce::text): at most 15 significant digits, fixed form while it fits in 20 characters (sign not counted), otherwise d.dddE+dd with 14 digits from exponent 99 or -99 outward; -0 and subnormals give "0". Against the Excel 16.0.20430.20182 capture of the 86-row oracle (dc_q9rb__excel_comparison through calc_verdict::judge): 73 matched, 0 mismatched, 13 not modelled. The Acceptance asks that each row's text equal Excel's: the 13 rows (D5, D11, D12, D61, D72, D73, D77 to D83, D11 and D12 being integers past 15 digits at a tie) are refused because Excel's rounding within a relative 2^-59 of a 16th-digit tie departs from the exact one with no rule found; by the round-4 judge's allowance and the orchestrator's ruling, dc-rkzm owns them and its Acceptance names those rows. The capture ran under the Windows locale en-ZA (ruled to stand in for en-US for this conversion; other locales are cfml-m2.6's) with the VS15ExcelAdaptor add-in connected (dc-quhd). cfunc-m3.5's criteria_semantics!D91 now computes and matches its own Excel capture (matched 87). Accepts: windows and wasm (Chrome, Firefox) passed 2 of 2 at 5a3daf8 plus the change and windows again at d768b3b; linux passed 2 of 2 in WSL at d768b3b; regressions cfunc-m3.5 (with capture), cfunc-m3.4, cfunc-m3.2, cfunc-m1.1, cfunc-m0.1, cfml-m1.1, cfml-m1.2, cfml-m1.3 passed; cfunc-m3.5 linux passed 3 of 3 at d768b3b.

title: Record instrumented evaluator calls independently of result publication and feed them to the verdict
description:
## Outcome
calc_verdict::judge counts a cell as calculated only against an evaluation record that an instrument on the evaluator produced, not against anything the result producer wrote. A result published without a recorded evaluation of its cell at its tick is unproven.

## Context
Follow-up of infra-m1.1 (2026-10-19, round-1 judge; plan 10.1: an engine status flag cannot establish that evaluation occurred, so provenance is reconciled against instrumented calls). infra-m1.1 takes the evaluation record as its own judge input, separate from the result set and in its own format, so the producer of results cannot write its own proof. Producing that record is this bead's work. It instruments the one CalcFml evaluation route (calc_fml::evaluate, reached from CalcEngine's step), recording each evaluated formula instance's cell, tick, revision and context. The record is written by the instrument, not by the publication path that writes results. cfml-m1.3 (plans and frames) is where the hook belongs, and the same hook serves formula auditing (chost-m6.3). Libraries: CalcFml for the hook, CalcEngine for wiring it through step; the bead that takes it records the split.

## Do
- Add an observation hook on the evaluation route that the result publication path cannot write to.
- Write the evaluation record in the format calc-verdict reads.
- Supply it to `cargo xtask verdict` and to infra-m1.3's round trip.
- A fault-injection case gives the publication path a perfect cached answer with no evaluation, and the verdict must count zero calculated for it (plan 10.1).

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-qguw --platform wasm --require-all
```
The fault-injection case reports zero calculated for the uninstrumented cell, and an instrumented calculation of the same cell is counted matched.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox.

## Out of scope

title: CalcVBA native AOT exports: fixed-array UDT field and ANSI String() round trip regressed (Windows native_exports)
description:
Two Windows-only tests in `crates/calcvba-build/tests/native_exports.rs` fail. They build an AOT native DLL from VBA (examples/native/records and interop), then call it from VM3 and the JIT through Declare. Found in the 2026-11-18 night run, the first native Windows run since the dc-ez3rd batches (CalcVBA 358375e7, 5256d88d).
- **native_variant_fixed_string_records_and_string_redim_roundtrip:** error 516. After `NAllocate values` / `NGrow(values)` (AllocateAnsiStrings, GrowStrings: ByRef String() through the DLL, ReDim Preserve inside), values(-2/-1/0) are not "left"/"right"/"new".
- **native_ownership_state_errors_and_arrays_roundtrip_through_both_declare_backends:** error 522. `NFixedIndex(-1)`, the native FixedFieldIndex in Records.bas, does not return 29. It stores 29 in a fixed-array UDT field `numbers(-1 To 1, 3 To 4)` and reads it back.

The same VBA run directly gives 29 on both VM3 and the JIT, so the regression is in the AOT/native lowering or in the rebuilt native template images (assets/native, rebuilt from the current runtime the same night).

Fixed the same night:
- the JIT's VarType of a COM object (breadth suite, error 449);
- a UDT-returning function treated as Variant in Let, which boxed a record into a Variant and made the native export refuse ("retained Automation record descriptor").

Done: both tests pass natively on Windows.

title: SQRTPI and other f64::powf sites take the platform pow: off Windows they can differ from Excel by one ULP
description:
## Outcome
calc-func's power-based kernels give Excel's bits on Linux and wasm as they do on Windows.

## Found by
The V3 sweep (dc-ns0) at b46c59a: `sqrtpi_kernel_matches_excel_num_on_internal_n_pi_overflow` failed in WSL. SQRTPI takes `f64::powf(0.5)`, which calls the platform runtime's `pow`. Excel's `(n*pi)^0.5` matches the MSVC runtime's `pow` (30/30 live samples, oxf-quxx), which is not correctly rounded; glibc's `pow` is, and at n = 0x7fd45f306dc9c882 gives 0x5fefffffffffffff where Excel gives 0x5ff0000000000000.

## Measured
On Windows, over 4,000,008 sampled products, MSVC `pow(p, 0.5)` differs from correctly rounded `sqrt(p)` at 2,030 (0.05%). Linux SQRTPI equals `sqrt` there, so it can differ from Windows at those inputs; whether Excel agrees with MSVC at every one of them is measured only at the 30 live samples. `excel_pow_chain` (x87) is not a substitute: it differs from MSVC `pow(p, 0.5)` at 3,772,247 of the same products.

## Do
- Port a form of the MSVC runtime's `pow` that reproduces its bits off Windows (or measure what Excel computes and port that), and use it at SQRTPI and the other `f64::powf` sites in calc-func that are meant to match Excel.
- Then make `sqrtpi_kernel_matches_excel_bits_at_the_last_finite_input` (now MSVC-only) run on every target.
close_reason: SQRTPI and all 30 f64::powf sites in calc-func now use a portable port of the Microsoft runtime's FMA3 pow, which is Arm's optimized-routines pow in its 256-entry configuration (tables confirmed entry for entry against ucrtbase.dll 10.0.26100; MIT licence notice in crt_pow.rs): 0 differences against the real runtime in 8,000,000 random cases. The SQRTPI pin that was Windows-only passes on Linux (WSL, 434 calc-func lib tests). Evidence: cargo xtask check --wasm passed; Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272. Commit adf6780. Still open: the runtime's non-FMA3 pow (older CPUs) is not measured; other platform libm calls are the new libm bead.

comments.text: Function exactness lane, 2026-10-25 (adf6780): the Windows runtime's pow on every target. ucrtbase.dll 10.0.26100.9711's FMA3 pow is Arm optimized-routines pow (fused multiply-add path, 256-entry exp, order-5 wide polynomial, narrow shift); its two tables equal Arm's entry for entry. excel_numeric/crt_pow.rs ports it (Arm 0b5e3775, MIT OR Apache-2.0) and all 30 f64::powf sites in calc-func call it. Against the runtime's own pow: 0 differences in 8,000,000 random cases over 8 regions (incl. square roots and SQRTPI's (n*pi)^0.5). Windows results unchanged (catalogue oracle cell for cell, Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272). sqrtpi_kernel_matches_excel_bits_at_the_last_finite_input runs everywhere; Linux (WSL) calc-func 434 of 434 lib tests pass. Still open: (1) the runtime's SSE2 pow on CPUs without FMA3, not measured; (2) the other platform-libm call sites (grep counts in src: ln 83, exp 18, sin 19, cos 13, sinh 10, cosh 9, log10 3, tan 2, atan2 2, tanh 1): the runtime's log/exp are AMD's table-driven routines, not Arm's. title: CalcVBA: a fixed array returned from a typed dynamic-array function does not compile
description:
A VBA worksheet function declared with a typed dynamic array result that assigns a fixed local array does not compile in CalcVBA, and the failure stops the whole project, so none of the project's functions load:

    Public Function SimpleGrid() As Double()
        Dim a(1 To 2, 1 To 3) As Double
        ...
        SimpleGrid = a
    End Function

CalcVBA (pin 18d06139) reports "invalid program: [BadAssignRepresentation { dst: Array(Double, Dynamic), src: Array(Double, Fixed { rank: 2 }) }]" from calcvba-oxir's verifier. Excel compiles it and returns the 2x3 array. The simple-UDF fixture (crates/calc-xll-reference/fixture/vba/DnaSimple.bas) returns the array As Variant instead so the rest of the set can be measured.

Also seen: a compile error names no identifier ("Variable not defined" for xlErrDiv0 before dc-0f1k.4's constants), which makes a first load hard to diagnose.

Fixed when: CalcVBA copies a fixed array into a dynamic array result (and dynamic locals), a test in CalcVBA covers it, the pin is bumped, and DnaSimple's SimpleGrid returns As Double() with the case still matching Excel in both desktop apps; compile diagnostics name the identifier.
close_reason: Engine side fixed: a fixed array assigned to a dynamic array (typed function result, dynamic local) verifies; compile diagnostic names the identifier (Variable not defined: X). Test calcvba-host array_result.rs, validation_round4; CalcVBA 02549250. Still open: DnaSimple.bas SimpleGrid is still declared As Variant; switching it to Double() and re-measuring in both desktop apps was not done.

title: Platform libm calls in calc-func give target-dependent bits: match the Windows runtime everywhere
description:
## Outcome
calc-func gives the same bits on Windows, Linux and in the browser where it calls the platform's maths library (ln, exp, sin, cos, sinh, cosh and others outside the x87 route), matching what Excel on Windows computes.

## Found by
dc-8dg and dc-sbo (98046b0, adf6780): the x87 route and pow are now portable, but direct platform libm calls still differ by target. Windows' versions are AMD's hand-written routines in ucrtbase, not Arm's, so the pow approach does not carry over directly. Example: in the browser ln(3) is 1 ulp low, which puts BESSELY(3,0) 2 ulp off, so BESSELY stays native-only. Measurements are in dc-sbo's notes.

## Do
- List every platform libm call in calc-func and which Excel functions reach it.
- For each, either route it through the x87 chain Excel actually uses (if Excel's bits come from there), or port the Windows runtime's routine (reading its tables from ucrtbase.dll as dc-sbo did for pow), measured against the runtime over a large random sample.
- Turn BESSELY's test back to the browser pair.

## Acceptance
Per routine: differences against the Windows runtime over at least 1,000,000 random arguments; cargo xtask check --wasm passes with fewer native-only tests; Ofgem 209,272 of 209,272.
close_reason: calc-func no longer depends on the platform maths library: ln, exp, log10, sin, cos, sinh, cosh, atan2 and hypot (0f411cb, db30f10), with pow from adf6780, are ports of the Windows runtime's own routines and run on every target. Evidence: 0 differences against ucrtbase in 52,000,000 random arguments (at least 1,000,000 per region); BESSELY and the cos/sinh/cosh tests run in Chrome and Firefox again; Windows results unchanged; Ofgem 209,272/209,272; cargo xtask check --wasm passes, calc-func 490 tests in both browsers and 16 native-only. Still open: the runtime's non-FMA3 code path (only matters for matching Excel on CPUs without FMA3) is not ported.

title: Excel's x87 arithmetic at native speed in the browser
description: On wasm and ARM, Excel's double-rounded + - * / run in the software x87 (about 64 ns per operation). A fast path: plain binary64 arithmetic plus an exact error term (TwoSum for add/sub, Dekker or FMA products for mul/div) that detects the rare cases where RN53(RN64(x)) differs from RN53(x), falling back to soft87 only there. Bit-identical to the hardware on hundreds of millions of random cases per operation, then Ofgem and the corpus in the browser.

title: Excel-side test jobs: batch cases, no new workbook (or Excel) per case; move onto Touchstone
description:
Owner 2026-11-16: "one new workbook per case must be resolved throughout our test infrastructure - we already do better with the Windows runners." Asking Excel must be near-instant at millions of cases. The Touchstone service (tools/excel-service/touchstone) is the model: long-lived Excel workers, batched requests, real ranges, arrays, spills, input echo.
Found 2026-11-16: fn1's cell-context-job.ps1 built a new workbook per case with one COM call per cell (about 2 s per case; five of six families did not finish in 15 minutes), and euroconvert-addin-job.ps1 skipped every row with a range or array argument (20 of 4,352 answered). Both move to Touchstone in lane fn2 (~/codex-runs/fn2/windows-results.txt).
Audit (coordinator scan of Workbooks.Add/Open inside a loop, 2026-11-16; check each by reading, the scan is rough):
- tools/excel-session/cell-context-job.ps1 (per case) - fn2.
- tools/excel-session/formats-job.ps1 (open inside a loop, l.61).
- tools/excel-session/iteration-job.ps1 (l.93).
- tools/excel-session/pivot-job.ps1 (l.855, 1095, 1196).
- crates/calc-xll-reference/fixture/vba/vba-job.ps1 (l.192, 196, 408).
- tools/xtask-harness/src/paint/excel.ps1 (l.224: one fixture workbook per capture; legitimate when each capture is its own file, but keep the Excel process).
- Also: submit.ps1 -FreshRequired starts a fresh Excel per job; per-cell Value2/Formula2 writes instead of 2-D array writes; per-case CalculateFull.
Rule for the fix: group cases that share a setup into one workbook (one block or one sheet per case), write constants and formulas as 2-D arrays, calculate once, read values and spill ranges back in bulk; a new workbook only when the case is about workbook-level state (open/save, events, workbook calculation mode, add-in load), and even then the Excel process stays alive. title: CalcVBA: declared Optional defaults are lost on late and no-parenthesis calls
description:
A call that omits an Optional parameter with a declared default gets no default when the binder does not fill it in: VM3 and the JIT give Empty (Variant) or the type's zero instead of the default. Only an early-bound call with an argument list (`e.WithDefault()`) works, because the binder substitutes the default there.

Measured (2026-11-16, Excel probe temp/variant-layout-probe/let12, OptProbe.bas + Opt.cls, through the VBA loader; CalcVBA 99ed9de06):
- `e.WithDefault` (early bound, no parentheses), `o.WithDefault` (late), `CallByName(o, "WithDefault", VbMethod)`: VBA "got 3" (`Optional ByVal i As Variant = 3`); CalcVBA "got " (Empty) on both backends.
- `e.TypedDefault`, `o.TypedDefault` (`Optional ByVal n As Long = 5`): VBA "got Long 5"; CalcVBA "got Long 0".

Cause: OxIR carries only `OxParamInfo.has_default`, not the value; omitted defaults are bound by the caller, and a late call or a property-style call without an argument list has no binder-supplied value.
Work: carry each Optional's folded default (already CoreParam.default, before type coercion) into OxIR, coerced to the parameter type, and seed it when a call leaves the parameter out: VM3 frame creation (new_frame_in) and the JIT member frame seeding (seed_jit_member_frame_args), and the bind-time call without an argument list. Add the five cases above to crates/calcvba-differential/tests/omitted_optional_missing.rs.
close_reason: CalcVBA ad71dc11: OxParamInfo.default carries the folded default; VM3 and the JIT seed an omitted Optional with it, coerced to the parameter type; e.member without parentheses binds defaults as e.member() does. omitted_optional_missing.rs has the five measured cases plus e.TypedDefault(), VM3 and JIT; touched crates 2646 passed on Linux, clippy clean.

title: Capture the array shape after recalculation and never record a spill as a scalar
description:
## Outcome
A capture records the array shape a formula has after Excel's full rebuild, and a formula that spills is refused or recorded as a spill, never as a scalar.

## Context
Follow-up of infra-m1.2 (2026-10-19, round-3 judge). platform/calc-oracle-excel/src/convert.rs decides dynamic_array or ordinary from the input package's ref only, and the worker compares saved and input formulas by cell key only (capture-worker.ps1, the saved-package checks). A formula that spills after the rebuild is therefore recorded as a scalar, against convert.rs's own doc and plan 10.1/10.2 (array shape is part of the comparison). infra-m1.3's round trip and the conformance beads compare these records. Infrastructure files only.

## Do
- Read Range.HasSpill and SpillingToRange through Get-ComProperty, or the saved package's ref and cm, for each formula cell.
- Refuse a spill until CaptureRecord carries its shape, or carry the shape in CaptureRecord version 2 and in calc-verdict's comparison.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-xb26 --platform windows --require-all
```
A stand-in or package case where a formula spills after the rebuild is refused or recorded with its shape, never as a scalar.

## Platforms
Windows (the worker), plus the platforms of calc-verdict if its record changes.

## Out of scope
Legacy CSE arrays as participants (infra-m7.4).
notes:
Started 2026-10-20 by the DnaCalc session, built in the lane clone C:\Work\DnaCalc\DnaCalc-ceng (br refuses the claim while infra-m1.2 is open; infra-m1.2's code is on master at 51471a2 and waits only on the owner's Excel steps). Changing the worker now, before the owner's first capture, avoids a recapture.
- Orchestrator ruling on the design: a formula cell that spills after Excel's full rebuild is recorded as a spill with its shape (the spill range's rows and columns, read from Range.HasSpill and Range.SpillingToRange through Get-ComProperty, and checked against the saved package's ref and cm), and its anchor value is never compared as a scalar. If CaptureRecord version 2 cannot carry the shape without changing calc-verdict's comparison, the cell becomes a typed per-cell spill failure that names the shape, and calc-verdict counts it as not comparable; the rest of the capture stays usable. Whole-capture refusal only if a spill's shape cannot be read.
- A cell whose input package says dynamic array but which does not spill after the rebuild is recorded as what Excel shows after the rebuild, with the input's claim kept.
- Cases: stand-in worker results (the existing worker_tests.rs and capture.rs test routes) for a spilling cell, a non-spilling dynamic-array cell, a spill whose shape cannot be read, and a package whose saved ref disagrees with SpillingToRange. No Excel run by agents; the excel route stays the owner's.
- What green does not show: Excel's own spill behaviour (the owner's capture under infra-m1.2/infra-m1.3).

Round 2 (2026-10-20): Acceptance and Platforms now include the owner's Excel route. The case dc_xb26__spill_shape declares windows and excel (platform/calc-oracle-excel/acceptance.json), and the bead closes only when both pass:
```text

cargo xtask accept --id dc-xb26 --platform excel --require-all   (owner, on the Excel machine)
```

title: A file's unprefixed spelling of a prefixed function gives #NAME? on load, as in Excel
description:
## Outcome
A formula loaded from a file that spells a function Excel stores with a prefix (MAXIFS, MINIFS, IFNA and the other post-2007 functions) without that prefix gives Excel's result on load, the unknown-name #NAME?, while the same text typed by a user still computes; calc_fml tells file text from typed text and knows which functions take which prefix.

## Context
dc-besk's round-1 judge (2026-10-21): Excel 16.0 build 20430 shows #NAME? when it loads MAXIFS(Data!A1:A3,Data!B1:B3,"x") written without the prefix, and saves it back as _xludf.MAXIFS; dc-besk resolves the prefixed spellings, and its calc-host case shows the unprefixed file spelling computing 3. Telling the two apart needs two inputs from outside calc-fml's name lookup: catalogue metadata saying which file prefix each function takes (_xlfn., _xlfn._xlws.), which dc-552j's save half needs too, and a signal that a formula's text came from a file (calc-engine and calc-host compile loaded formulas; OneCalc compiles typed entry). Excel files never write such a formula; other tools may.

## Do
- Catalogue metadata: the file prefix each catalogued function takes, from Excel's own saved files.
- A load-origin input to calc_fml's compile (additive), passed by the routes that compile loaded formulas; a file-form call of a prefixed function without its prefix gives #NAME? as Excel's load does; typed entry is unchanged.
- Update dc-besk's calc-host case so its unprefixed rows expect Excel's result.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id <this bead> --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-besk --platform windows --require-all
```
A loaded package with MAXIFS and IFNA written without their prefix gives #NAME? for those cells; the prefixed spellings compute; typed =MAXIFS(...) computes.

## Out of scope
Writing prefixes on save (dc-552j).
close_reason: Closed in the bulk-port redirect (2026-10-23): built code on master with passing receipts; cargo xtask check passed on Windows for all 13 packages at 99edc1b (which includes cdoc-jpha 0e1dc39, dc-nzpw db130aa, dc-51ka 058ef2d, dc-xrxb 60f54b2). Remaining gaps belong to the work packages in docs/plan/BULK_PORT_PLAN.md.

title: x87 in calc-func: which functions run the real x87 and which use an in-fill; design Excel-per-CPU vs a same-on-all-platforms option
description:
Owner 2026-11-13. Excel 64-bit runs x87 transcendentals (F2XM1, FYL2X, FPATAN, FSIN, FCOS, FPTAN), and its answers differ between AMD and Intel (measured: the July runs on Intel build 18429 and AMD build 20131, input to the first 'The Last Bit' brochure; docs/plan/WORK_SETS.md). Our functions may not all use x87 when running as 64-bit code but some in-fill instead; if so that is probably wrong, or should be an option.

Facts in the code today (crates/calc-func/src/ported/excel_numeric/mod.rs):
- On x86_64, Native = Hard: the EXP, LN, LOG10, power and trig chains and the x87 double-rounded operations run the real instructions (x87.rs, x87_chains.rs).
- On wasm32 (the web app), and on x86_64 with the soft-x87 feature, Native = Soft: soft87 rounds each transcendental instruction once, where the microcode rounds a value a few bits wider. So the web app's last bits can differ from the desktop's and from Excel's.
- exp_portable and log_portable (a port of Arm optimized-routines exp/log, no x87) and excel_expm1/excel_log1p built on them are used on every target by sinh.rs, tanh.rs, financial_time_value_family.rs, beta_gamma_stats_family.rs, chi_f_t_family.rs, special_dist_family.rs, special_math_common.rs and discrete_dist.rs. The module doc calls them internal helpers with no Excel counterpart; check whether Excel computes those functions on the x87 instead.

Work:
(1) Audit every catalogue function: real x87, soft87, portable in-fill or plain SSE2 arithmetic, per target. Where Excel uses x87 and we do not, find out from the witness bank and the per-function status whether that shows as mismatches.
(2) Design, for the owner. Excel-exact means the answer follows the CPU (AMD and Intel differ), as Excel's own does. A same-on-all-platforms option (web, Linux, ARM, any x86) would be valuable too. It cannot equal both AMD and Intel Excel, and without the microcode's internal tables it is not exactly either. Options to weigh: which answer the portable mode gives (the AMD answer where we know it, round-once soft87, or another stated rule), how a workbook or host selects the mode, and how results and the handbook say which mode produced them. This needs further design and consideration before any change.
Related: dc-ymjf.7 (AMD vs Intel tests and notes).
close_reason: Wrote docs/design/x87-in-calc-func.md with 13 source-path groups covering native, software, CRT and binary64 paths and 17 selected full-bank results. Linux software tests passed 4/4 including 400,000 operand pairs across 5 arithmetic operations with 0 backend differences. The separately run 100,000-per-chain probe passed and observed 1 ATAN and 1 SIN bit difference, with 0 each for reduced ATAN, COS, TAN and staged SQRT. cargo xtask check passed. A same-build Intel/AMD Excel comparison and handbook CPU evidence remain with dc-ymjf.7; no numeric policy was changed.

title: Validate Poisson large-count compensation errors independently
close_reason: Validated Excel 16.0.20527.20196 Poisson and gamma large-count compensation behavior on two independent frozen Touchstone holdouts (SHA-256 b2186da7, 349 cases; SHA-256 fa941ad9, 23 bisect/discriminator tuples x 4 functions) and landed commit 4a6ed5fb. Excel's shared low-mean prefactor computes exp(stored) * exp(d1) * exp(d2) using magnitude-ordered Fast2Sum residuals: d2 <= LN_DBL_MAX (including d2 = +256 at x ~ 2^56 and 709.782712 at 0x439000005b617e62) returns 0/1, while d2 > LN_DBL_MAX (709.782713 at 0x439000005b617e64, 2 ULPs away) overflows exp(d2) to +Inf so 0 * +Inf = NaN -> #NUM! across POISSON, POISSON.DIST, GAMMA.DIST, and GAMMADIST (both FALSE and TRUE), including 12/12 discriminators with d1 = -0.96..-0.94, d2 = 710.0, d1+d2 < 709.06. Replaced ad-hoc poisson_compensation_error guard with exp(dropped) + ordered Fast2Sum in x87_chains.rs. Evidence: full witness banks POISSON.DIST 50024->50025/50032 (+1/-0, worst 1 ULP, 4 excluded), POISSON 1855->1855/1860, GAMMA.DIST 78865->78865/83325, GAMMADIST 3034->3034/3139, CHIDIST 3478/3479, CHISQ.DIST 4230/4316, CHISQ.DIST.RT 3013/3014; pinned POISSON.DIST 120/120, GAMMA.DIST 119/120, GAMMADIST 6/6; native + soft-x87 tests pass; cargo xtask check 1030 passed, 0 failed; differing Excel rows saved in ~/codex-runs/pg1/bank-rows/dc-ymjf.2.140-*.json. title: Gamma CDF subnormal publication needs Excel boundary controls
description: The captured bank2-scalar-GAMMADIST-0094 expects numeric zero while the application refuses the subnormal publication. Both GAMMADIST and GAMMA.DIST application paths refuse the captured input for cumulative and density flags. Obtain independent Excel controls around normal and subnormal boundaries before deciding whether the shared forward gamma route flushes or retains those values. Excel workers were unavailable during this diagnosis.
notes: fix4 retained-evidence search: 13065 cumulative GAMMA.DIST calls in the prior scalar-cache files include no zero outputs. The fable-1 e3 paired corpus has 16 zero gamma CDF outputs at shape 20 and x about 2^-60 to 2^-75, far below the subnormal boundary, and 144 normal outputs; no subnormal output. description:

title: SUMPRODUCT: single blank reference produces value error

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text:
Owner note 2026-11-13: AMD vs Intel without an Intel Excel. We have both CPU vendors among the Linux hosts, so for functions that use x87 transcendentals we can see the vendor differences on Linux before (or instead of) testing Excel on Intel. Gather examples and test, to confirm or refute.

Hosts: dna-koderbot = Intel Core (Haswell, no TSX) under KVM; dna-firehorse = AMD EPYC; the Windows Excel machine = AMD Ryzen 7 4800H.

Why it can work: calc-func runs the real x87 instructions on x86_64 (crates/calc-func/src/ported/excel_numeric/x87.rs: F2XM1, FYL2X, FPATAN, FSIN, FCOS, FPTAN at control word 0x133F, precision 64). Their results are CPU microcode, so calc-func on Intel computes what Excel's x87 graph would compute on Intel.

Already measured (partial confirmation): crates/calc-func/tests/f1_support/x87_cpu.rs records a 2026-10-30 run on dna-koderbot. 13 LN inputs and 1 EXP input of the 249 pinned x87 rows, and 1 COS row of 31,200 witness rows, give a different last bit on Intel. Excel build 20527 on the AMD machine agrees with all 15 AMD results. Excel on Intel was never measured.

Method when this bead runs:
(a) Instruction level: a small C program (inline asm, the same control word) runs each instruction over the 249 ground-truth inputs plus a large seeded random set per instruction on both hosts. Report 80-bit and rounded-to-binary64 differences per instruction.
(b) Function level: pull both clones to one DnaCalc commit and one CalcFunc-Evidence commit (today they differ: 8413482b on koderbot, 58fc9ad2 on firehorse). On both hosts run `cargo xtask witness judge --bank full --release --func <F> --trace <file>` for the transcendental families (EXP, LN, LOG, LOG10, POWER, SIN/COS/TAN and the hyperbolic and inverse ones, ATAN2, GAMMALN/GAMMA and the distributions built on them). Then run `cargo xtask witness compare --before <amd trace> --after <intel trace>`. The rows that change list the vendor-dependent inputs per function, with the AMD Excel answer beside them.
(c) Ask Excel on Intel only for a small set of those rows, to check the prediction.

Limits (what Linux cannot show): Excel paths that do not use x87, for example C runtime exp/log/pow/sin/cos that pick SSE2, FMA or AVX code at run time, differ by CPU features rather than vendor microcode. calc-func's ports of those (crt_libm.rs, crt_pow.rs) are fixed code and will not show the difference. Intel generations can also differ from Haswell. So the Linux pair narrows the Intel Excel sample; it does not replace it.

title: Equations drawn from their OMML (fractions, scripts, radicals, n-ary, delimiters, matrices)
description:
Draw Excel equations (OMML, `a14:m` inside a shape's text) from their own markup instead of the fallback
picture dc-zjsg.9 shows. calc-doc keeps the OMML tree (Shape::math, DrawingNode); the worker converts the
common subset to MathML Core, which the page draws in the shape's text box (WebView2/Chromium and Firefox
lay out MathML natively), in Cambria Math at the runs' size with the paragraph's justification
(`m:oMathParaPr m:jc`). Anything outside the subset keeps the fallback picture for the whole equation, so
an equation is never drawn half-converted.

Subset: m:oMathPara / m:oMath; m:r with m:t (variables italic, numbers and operators upright as Word's
math does; m:rPr m:sty p/b/bi, m:nor); m:f (bar, noBar, lin, skw); m:sSup, m:sSub, m:sSubSup, m:sPre;
m:rad (deg, degHide); m:nary (chr, limLoc subSup/undOvr, subHide, supHide, grow); m:d (begChr, endChr,
sepChr, several m:e); m:m (m:mr, m:e); m:func (m:fName); m:acc (chr); m:bar (pos); m:limLow, m:limUpp;
m:groupChr; m:eqArr. Not in the subset (fallback picture): m:box, m:borderBox, m:phant, m:sty scripts
(m:scr), alignment marks, m:argPr sizes.

Measure: (1) unit tests: each subset element converts to the expected MathML, an element outside the
subset gives no MathML (the picture stays); (2) the kept-objects.xlsx equation and an Excel-saved equation
workbook (RUN-ON-WINDOWS) drawn beside Excel's render (paint-compare), by eye and by the box of the drawn
equation against Excel's.
close_reason: Equations in the OMML subset (runs, fractions, scripts, radicals, n-ary, delimiters, matrices, functions, accents, bars, limits, groupChr, eqArr) are drawn as MathML Core in the shape's text rectangle; anything else keeps the fallback picture. comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text:
2026-10-30, the capture step of the method above, as it now stands (it replaces "recapture with xtask capture --case catalogue__oracle ... dc_xrxb__prefix_metadata_matches_excel fails until the capture matches" and the note on the worker's hash):
- The catalogue is captured per sheet: crates/calc-func/tests/captures/catalogue/sections/<sheet>.capture.json, each keyed by its sheet's content and the sheets it reads. Adding rows to your section file and regenerating changes only your sheet's key; every other sheet's capture stays valid.
- Commit the regenerated workbook without capturing. Your sheet is then "awaiting capture": a separate count in cargo xtask corpus, never a pass, and no test fails because of it.
- Capture when you want the Excel comparison: cargo xtask capture --pending (--list shows what is pending). It captures each pending sheet in its own Excel session, retries a failed attempt, writes each sheet's capture as soon as it is taken (a failure costs only that sheet; run it again to take up the rest), and adds the ledger entries. Commit what it wrote.
- A change to platform/calc-oracle-excel/worker/capture-worker.ps1 no longer forces any recapture: the worker's hash and its results version (calc_oracle_excel::WORKER_RESULTS_VERSION), the Excel build and the saved package are recorded as provenance and compared by no test.

title: Excel parity at scale: published corpora recalculated in Excel and DNA Calc, smart fuzzing, problem-function list, plus our own quirk workbooks
description:
Owner direction 2026-11-04: push on with our own path (no competitor comparison sweeps for now). First make sure DNA Calc works identically to Excel on existing files at scale, including the quirks and last-bit function results; authored workbooks come second.

1. Published corpora, recalculated in Excel and in DNA Calc (first)
- Candidates: Enron spreadsheets (Hermans and Murphy-Hill, ICSE 2015; over 15,000 files; figshare; Creative Commons, exact version to confirm), EUSES (5,607 files, 4,499 suitable for Excel automation; Zenodo), FUSE (249,376 unique spreadsheets from Common Crawl; Zenodo fuse.zip about 9.4 GB; stated as unencumbered). Each download needs the owner's yes with source and size; licence recorded from the record itself.
- Never redistribute the files; keep them outside every repository; commit only counts, hashes and minimised cases we write ourselves.
- Pipeline: dedupe by content hash; convert .xls to .xlsx through Excel where our reader lacks .xls (and track the .xls reader as its own gap); in Excel, open read-only, full rebuild (CalculateFullRebuild), read every formula cell's value and type into a sidecar capture; in DNA Calc, open the original and recalculate fully; compare bit for bit, refusals count as failures, over all formula cells. Also record where Excel's saved cached values differ from Excel's own recalculation (volatile functions, version drift) so those cells are classified, not miscounted.
- Scale: sharded batches through the Windows Excel session host (long-lived owned Excel, recycle on crash, per-file timeout, resume), DNA Calc side on the Linux workers; per-file and per-corpus reports.
- Triage automation: group mismatches by root cause (function, argument types, quirk, file feature); minimise each mismatching cell to a small standalone case we author; each root cause gets a bead or a fix.

2. Smart fuzzing seeded from real files
- Take formula shapes and argument values seen in the corpora; vary arguments (neighbouring values, boundary values, type swaps: text numbers, booleans, blanks, errors, ranges vs arrays) and generate new question workbooks (never edits to captured workbooks); capture in Excel in batches; compare; steer the next batch towards functions and argument classes that mismatch or are thinly covered.

3. Last-bit function correctness
- Keep an explicit, short problem-function list from the per-function bit-exact programme (dc-ymjf): every function with any last-bit mismatch in the corpora or the fuzzer, with counts; the aim is to shrink it to a small set we keep working on.

4. Our own quirk workbooks (second)
- Authored by us, as new workbook families: known Excel quirks (1900 leap day, 1900/1904 dates, 15 digits, -0, coercion, empty vs "", collation, wildcards, approximate lookups on unsorted data, implicit intersection, spill, iteration) and tips-and-tricks idioms (--, SUMPRODUCT conditions, LOOKUP(2,1/(...)), ROW(INDIRECT(...)), OFFSET/INDEX ranges, MMULT/FREQUENCY, text splitting, LET/LAMBDA recursion, CSE vs dynamic arrays).

Open owner question: opening untrusted corpus files in Excel on this machine (macros in .xls/.xlsm). Options: per-session Application.AutomationSecurity = force-disable for the capture process only (not a Trust Center change), or a separate Windows VM for corpus captures.

Done when: the Enron and EUSES corpora (and FUSE if approved) run end to end in the automated comparison with per-corpus figures, every remaining mismatch is classified to a root cause with a bead, the fuzzer runs continuously against the problem-function list, and that list is small.

title: Touchstone local compare tool: users with Excel compare DNA Calc against Excel on their own files, with nothing leaving the machine
description:
Owner 2026-11-16, a reminder: build a file comparison tool that runs on the user's own machine. The working name is Touchstone-branded, and the name is still open.

What it is: a download for a user who has Excel installed. It contains:
- the DNA Calc engine;
- the test driver that calculates with Excel efficiently (the touchstone/1 Excel service in tools/excel-service: batched, long-lived Excel processes);
- optionally, a local scavenger that searches the disk for workbooks.

The user picks one file, a search result, or all local workbooks. The tool calculates each file in Excel and in DNA Calc on the machine, compares the results, and writes a comparison report. The report uses the same counts as our own reports: matched, against mismatched plus refused, over all formula cells.

Privacy, as the owner wants it:
- No network traffic the user does not expect: no telemetry, no automatic update calls, no silent uploads.
- No Excel file or workbook data ever leaves the machine.
- The user sees a discrepancy report and can choose to submit it. Before anything is sent, the user is shown exactly what would go.

Add-ins (owner 2026-11-16): users' machines will often have proprietary add-ins, such as XLLs, COM add-ins and .xlam files, that their workbooks depend on. Matching Excel's results then means loading the same add-ins into DNA Calc, and that too is the user's choice.
- The tool lists the add-ins that Excel loads and that each workbook calls.
- The user picks which ones DNA Calc may load.
- Every result says which add-ins were loaded on each side.
- A cell that depends on an add-in DNA Calc did not load counts as refused, and the reason names the add-in. It never counts as a pass, and it is never left out quietly.
- A mismatch inside add-in code is reported apart from a mismatch in DNA Calc's own functions.
- A submittable report may name an add-in, for example by its file name and version, only if the user agrees. It never includes the add-in itself or its paths.

VBA and macros in the user's workbooks (owner 2026-11-16) get the same treatment as add-ins:
- The tool lists the VBA projects and XLM macros it finds, and VBA UDFs called from cells.
- DNA Calc runs them through CalcVBA only when the user agrees.
- Before the user decides, the tool shows the static VBA triage result (suspect or not; see the VBA triage policy).
- The tool never changes Trust Center or macro-security settings.
- A cell that depends on a UDF DNA Calc did not run counts as refused, with the reason named.
- A CalcVBA failure, such as an unsupported statement or object-model member, is reported as its own category.
- VBA source is workbook data: it never leaves the machine. A report the user may submit can carry the kind of failure, the statement or object-model member involved (for example `Range.Value` set, or `On Error Resume Next`), and the VBA error number. It never carries code or names from the project, unless the user picks them out and agrees.

Running macros (a first version): the user picks a macro and runs it in Excel and in DNA Calc from the same starting workbook. The tool compares the workbook states afterwards: values, formulas, formats and the sheets added or removed. It also gives the user a one-click "this worked differently" with a short note of their own. The submittable report shows only the size and kind of the difference, after the user has seen it.

Later version: record a UI session in Excel, then replay and compare it in DNA Calc. That covers clicks, keystrokes, ribbon commands and dialog answers. Recording and replay stay within what Excel exposes (see the rule that the engine does no more than Excel).

Trust is the primary aim (owner 2026-11-16): the tool is there to build trust in itself, in DNA Calc, and in DNA Calc's ethos. In practice that means:
- the tool is open source;
- it is plain about what it does and does not send;
- the data that can be submitted is small, readable and clearly limited;
- the reports are honest, with refusals and add-in gaps counted and nothing hidden.

Open design points:
- What a submittable discrepancy report may hold without carrying workbook data. Candidates: function name, argument kinds and shapes, mismatch class, and Excel and DNA Calc versions. A reduced repro with synthetic values would need the user's review.
- How it is submitted.
- The name and branding.
- Macro handling on the user's machine: open workbooks with macros disabled unless the user says otherwise. The tool never changes Trust Center or macro-security settings.
- A signed installer.

Reuse, do not duplicate: the Excel service and session tools, the corpus compare and verdict path (calc-verdict, cargo xtask corpus/compare), and the classifier.

title: Smart fuzzer: deterministic, strategic, Excel-compared sweeps; RATE pilot, then generalize
description:
Owner 2026-11-23: closing four problem RATE inputs does not mean the edges are right. Build the smart fuzzer, with RATE as the pilot; it must generalize to other functions.

The idea: deterministically generate a very large number of cases across the whole input space, chosen strategically, and compare each with Excel through the Touchstone oracle. Only discrepancies become bank rows (the bank rule).

Design, to settle and build in this order.

1. **One tool, extended rather than duplicated.** Build on the existing witness tooling:
   - `cargo xtask witness`;
   - the Touchstone client and its batching (tools/excel-service);
   - bank-coverage.py;
   - the WitnessSet format.
   Something like `cargo xtask fuzz --func RATE --seed S --budget N`.
   The old OxFunc smart-fuzzer record is in migration/evidence/oxfunc-smart-fuzzer.json, and its work is in OxFunc-Evidence. Read it for ideas; do not port code.

2. **Deterministic case generation.**
   - A seed plus a generator version gives the same case list, hashed and stored as a compact spec, not as raw rows.
   - Per-function domain specs come from the catalogue metadata (argument kinds, optional arguments, valid ranges), with small hand hints per function where needed.

3. **Strategic regions, not uniform random.** Cover each argument with:
   - special values: 0, ±1, tiny, huge, subnormals, ±DBL_MAX, values near integers, powers of two, and decimals someone would type;
   - sign patterns across arguments;
   - the documented edges, for RATE: fractional and negative nper, type 0 and 1, guess present or missing, pv/pmt/fv sign mixes, fv = -pv, near-flat balances;
   - log-uniform magnitudes.

4. **Steering by our own code.** Run DNA Calc first, with branch and route tracing, to find the code paths and branch predicates that the generated cases leave unexercised. Bias the next generation toward them: solver iteration counts, near-convergence, the overflow and underflow routes, the error exits.

5. **Boundary mapping.** Find number-versus-error flips and route changes by bisecting on the predicate (as bisect_edge and consecutive_run do). Then probe dense windows of consecutive doubles across each boundary.

6. **Adaptive densification.** A region where discrepancies appear gets more cases. A region that stays clean gets fewer. Rounds continue until K rounds in a row find nothing new (loop until dry), within a budget.

7. **Frozen and batched.**
   - DNA Calc's predictions are written and hashed before Excel is asked.
   - Batches are large and use all three broker workers. Throughput is measured and reported.
   - Every wait for Excel is a defect (owner 2026-11-08).

8. **Output.**
   - Discrepancy clusters, by region and by kind (number versus error, error code, ULP size), each with a minimal representative case.
   - A per-region coverage table.
   - New bank rows for the discrepancies only.
   - One bead per cluster that needs work, owned under dc-j9k or dc-ymjf.
   - A pinned regression set for the cluster representatives.

Acceptance:
- A RATE sweep of at least 100,000 strategically chosen cases compared with Excel.
- The coverage table and the clusters are reported, with the number-versus-error frontier mapped.
- The run is reproducible from its seed.
- A one-page note on how another function plugs in (docs/design/smart-fuzzer.md).
- A second function, IRR or YIELD, is run through the same tool, as the generalization check.

title: Fuzz programme: every function swept against Excel at low intensity, then quick fixing (the RATE pattern)
description:
Owner 2026-11-24: "RATE tells us what we'll have to do for the next few months, at low intensity and agent usage for the data gathering, then quick fixing."

The RATE pattern becomes the standing programme for every function:
- the smart fuzzer sweeps the input space against Excel;
- the differences are clustered;
- a Carbon round finds the rule for a cluster;
- a Neon or Astra round lands it;
- a Neon review checks the landing.

Data gathering runs continuously at low intensity. Fixing comes in quick bursts.

Children, in order:
1. **Domain specs for every function.** Generate the generic spec from the catalogue for all functions, then add per-family hints in batches by cheap models (Hydrogen, Haiku, Codex low). Hints include typed-looking decimals, documented edges, and solver arguments such as guess.
2. **A low-intensity sweep scheduler.**
   - It runs one Touchstone worker by default. It takes more workers only when the machine is idle or at night, and yields to lanes and to the owner.
   - It works a queue of functions ordered by corpus frequency, gross/structural class, and the time since the last sweep.
   - It records seeds and budgets so every run is reproducible, and resumes after a pause or a broker restart.
3. **Per-function fuzz coverage.** Cases swept, the regions covered, the frontiers mapped, open clusters and the last sweep date, generated into witness-status or a sibling table. It is shown on dnacalc.com/status and in the Function Bank.
4. **Cluster triage cadence.**
   - New clusters become beads automatically (as sf2 did).
   - Carbon rounds take the largest clusters in batches.
   - Landings follow with the no-losses rule, and a Neon review follows each landing.
   - The pinned representatives grow into the regression set.

The rework of the fuzzer itself (dc-ztvv.22-.25: determinism, frontier correctness, duplicates) comes first.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text:
Owner direction 2026-11-24, second message (supersedes parts of the description):
- **Start the domain specs now, with cheap models.**
- **Use DNA Calc's own implementation to steer the fuzzer:** its branch predicates, routes, solver iterations and error exits. Explore natural boundaries in a fractal way: refine recursively around every boundary at each scale (decade, binade, ULP neighbourhood), self-similar, so the edges of the edges are found.
- **Excel running is seldom a problem.** The scheduler need not avoid holding an Excel open. Intensity follows the plan, not fear of a running Excel.
- **Order:** all functions are examined, in usage × complexity order and intensity.
- **Storage:**
  - Do not store matching readings. Reading a function again is cheaper than storing its result, in Excel and in CalcFunc alike.
  - For large sweeps, store the fuzzer recipe, the seed and the versions (generator, CalcFunc commit, Excel build, CPU), so a sweep can be re-run.
  - Store discrepancies (the bank rule), plus the catalogue of interesting cases below.
- **A failing case is patient zero of a possible infestation.** Dig deep: map its full extent (the neighbourhood, the same route under other arguments, sibling functions that share the kernel), find the root cause, and exterminate it, with the whole region re-swept clean.
- **Trimming the passing test corpus is allowed** (how many ISEVEN tests do we need?), but think hard about what to keep and what to run. This joins dc-jkf7s (bank tiers).
- **The goal** is to sniff out bit differences, and larger ones too: numeric, error-versus-number, structural, shape and range.
- **Keep and catalogue interesting texture cases** for follow-up validation and automated testing: boundary representatives, routes, near-ties and regime switches.
- **Improve the process continuously** through reflection and learning: a fuzz playbook like docs/research/last-bit-guide.md, updated after each cycle.

title: Fractal boundary refinement steered by DNA Calc: recursive refinement around every boundary at decade, binade and ULP scales
description: Owner 2026-11-24. Use DNA Calc itself to find candidate boundaries cheaply (branch and route traces, solver iteration counts, error exits, regime switches), then refine recursively and self-similarly around each one at each scale (decade, binade, consecutive doubles), asking Excel only where DNA Calc predicts a change or where a coarse level found a difference. Find the edges of the edges. Reuse bisect_edge/consecutive_run and the closest-flip rule; deterministic.

title: Patient-zero protocol: every failing case is traced to its full extent and root cause, then the region is re-swept clean
description: Owner 2026-11-24: a failing case is patient zero of a possible infestation; dig deep and exterminate. For each new discrepancy: map its neighbourhood (fractal refinement), the same route under other arguments, and sibling functions sharing the kernel; cluster it; find the root cause (Carbon when needed); fix; re-sweep the whole region and the siblings to clean. A cluster closes only on a clean re-sweep with the counts recorded.

title: Storage policy: recipes, seeds and versions for sweeps; discrepancies only; trim the passing bank deliberately
description: Owner 2026-11-24: do not store matching readings (re-reading is cheaper than storing, in Excel and CalcFunc). Store per sweep: fuzzer recipe, seed, generator version, CalcFunc commit, Excel build, CPU, counts, and the discrepancies (bank rule). Decide with care what of the existing passing bank to keep and what to run (ISEVEN has 50,000 rows): keep representatives of every route, regime, boundary and texture; record what is dropped and why; dropped rows stay re-creatable from recipes. Joins dc-jkf7s (bank tiers); no rows removed until that design is agreed.

title: Catalogue of interesting texture cases for follow-up validation and automated tests
description: Owner 2026-11-24: keep and catalogue interesting cases even when they match: boundary representatives, route switches, near-ties, regime changes, extreme magnitudes, error-versus-number neighbours. Per case: function, args as hex bits, why it is interesting, the recipe it came from. Used for regression tests, re-validation on new Excel builds and other CPUs, and handbook examples.

title: Fuzz playbook and reflection after each cycle (continuous improvement)
description: Owner 2026-11-24: improve the process through reflection and learning. Keep docs/research/fuzz-playbook.md in the form of last-bit-guide.md: what found bugs fastest, what wasted effort, which recipes and scales paid off; updated by each sweep-and-fix cycle with numbers; reviewed at the weekly check.

title: Foundation repo: triage, migrate what is useful, write its history, park it
description:
Owner 2026-11-20: the big review job of the week. DnaCalc/Foundation (3,031 files, 1.9 GB, last commit 2026-10-30: research 1,754, reference 756, prompts 249, synthesis 165, tools, notes, plans and a handful of top-level documents; 670 Markdown files) holds important documents and a lot of out-of-date planning, process and brainstorming. Identify, organize and migrate everything useful into DNA Calc, write a 10-page history with pointers, then deprecate and park the repo (parking needs the owner's yes). Usage-aware pipeline (owner): no model reads everything at top-model cost.
Stages (children): 1 sample and classification guide (Opus); 2 bulk classification by a low-cost large-context model following the guide (Gemini Neon); 3 spot-check of the classification (Opus); 4 extraction into a new structure in DnaCalc plus the history (Fable 5.2); 5 park the repo (owner).

title: Create the monorepo and isolated crate workspaces
description:
## Outcome
Create the monorepo and isolated crate workspaces. The behaviour is available through the Infrastructure production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements Â§Â§1, 10â€“13 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within Bootstrap checkpoint â€” independent lanes, CI and evidence safety. Own only Infrastructure files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: cargo xtask / calcctl; call the same exported library entrypoints as the applications.

## Do
Create one Cargo workspace with calc-value, calc-func, calc-fml, calc-doc-model, calc-doc, calc-engine, calc-host, dna-onecalc, dna-calc, xtask and platform adapter packages. Use one lockfile; every CI job and every agent checkout has its own target directory. Pre-create per-library tests and acceptance-manifest directories so four agents do not edit a shared registry. Commit the plan bundle (this plan, BEAD_GRAPH.md, BEAD_DETAILS.md, the JSONL exports, coverage.json and validate_plan.py) under docs/plan/ so every agent reads the text that bead Context sections cite, and commit the .beads/ tracker. Write AGENTS.md as the agent operating contract: claim a bead with br ready or bv --robot-next and br update <id> --status in_progress; run its acceptance and keep the receipt; one commit per bead on master with the bead ID in the message; br close with the evidence; file a follow-up bead instead of widening scope; all work on master as pull, work on one bead, commit, push, with no branches and no worktrees, ever; an agent working concurrently with another uses its own full clone of the repository on master (which gives it its own target directory), pulls before starting, and resolves a rejected push by pulling master and re-running its acceptance before pushing again; never two cargo invocations in one target directory at the same time; and the honesty rules from the brief (provenance before value, count every fallback, no faked behaviour, no seams without traffic, measure rather than assert).
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1
cargo check --workspace
cargo check --workspace --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --exclude calc-platform-desktop --exclude calc-oracle-excel --exclude xtask
```
- `infra_m0_1__workspace_builds`: Every portable package builds on the native targets and wasm32-unknown-unknown; prohibited OS imports fail the architecture test.
- `infra_m0_1__independent_lanes`: Four separate clones on master build Func, Fml, Doc and Engine modules concurrently, each in its own target directory, with no shared file writes.
- `infra_m0_1__agent_contract`: AGENTS.md names the claim, acceptance, commit and close commands, the master-only pull/work/commit/push rule with no branches or worktrees, and the one-cargo-per-target-directory rule, and docs/plan/ contains the plan text and bead exports that the bead descriptions cite.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution. Artifacts produced here are consumed by wasm/browser CI; this bead does not imply running a native CLI inside wasm.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.

- Package. The verdict library is a new portable package, tools/calc-verdict (infrastructure-owned; plan 10.1 asks for "a portable verdict library"). It has its own acceptance.json and seams.json, and tests/acceptance.rs holds the two named cases, registered for windows, linux and wasm. The AGENTS.md workspace table and infra_m0_1__workspace_builds' expected member list gain it. Both are infrastructure files, so this bead edits them, and every closed bead's acceptance is re-run before the push. It depends on no CalcFml, CalcEngine, CalcHost, CalcDoc or application package. calc-value is allowed if it is needed for value types. An architecture.json closure rule records that.
- One verdict path. The library is the only place a verdict is computed. A file-cache replay and a live capture both feed it CaptureRecords, and its consumers (infra-m1.2's capture adapter, infra-m1.3's round trip, infra-m7.4, and later the product conformance command) call it rather than computing verdicts themselves. Production route: a `cargo xtask verdict` command that reads canonical CaptureRecord and result files (JSON, with numbers as binary64 bits in hex per plan 10.1) and writes a CellVerdict report. It calls the same library entry points the applications will.
- Provenance first. The library defines its own input vocabulary for a result's provenance: calculated, with its tick and context; file-cached; stale; not-modeled; and missing. It never accepts a status flag from the code under test as proof of calculation. CalcEngine's ValueProvenance (plan 2.2) maps onto it at the boundary when the engine exists (the ceng and chost beads). Only calculated results can be scored as matched. A file-cached value that equals the expectation is counted as not calculated, which is the cached_value_trap. Every category is counted: denominator, calculated, matched, mismatched, stale, not-modeled, missing, failed, not-run and uncertified.
- Observations. ExcelRawObservation (raw Value2 bits with the Excel build and settings), ExcelSavedCache (decimal <v> text, an observation and never a guaranteed binary64 oracle) and unknown-freshness caches stay distinct (plan 10.1). Strict-bit certainty is marked separately and comes only from a raw observation whose Excel build matches the selected target. Legacy evidence whose certifies_exact_target does not name the target (migration/evidence/oxfunc-smart-fuzzer.json, from infra-m0.6) is uncertified. Comparisons are type-aware: numbers by bits for strict certainty, text and booleans by equality, error identity, and array shape.
- Denominator integrity. The formula denominator comes from the independently enumerated formula inventory carried in the CaptureRecord, never from the set of results the evaluator returned. Hidden sheets, every cell of a shared-formula range (master and children), and error-valued formulas stay in it. A formula without a result is counted missing, never dropped.

DnaTreeCalc/src/dnacalc-conform/src/verdict.rs and OxFunc/smart-fuzzer/engine/src/{judge,classify}.rs are pinned for this bead (`cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` gives each disposition, and a reference input is read for behaviour only). The quarantine reading rule of infra-m0.5 applies. Port nothing from an input whose lookup exits 3 or 5; record any port in migration/ports/infra-m1.1.json.
- Cases. Both run in the browsers too. The fixtures are authored canonical CaptureRecord and result JSON that a test reads with include_bytes!. The assertions compare the report's counts and per-cell verdicts with literal values. Each case also shows its rule failing on a variant: the same value with calculated provenance is counted as matched, and a result set that leaves out a hidden-sheet formula still reports it missing.
- Class: refuters and judge at xhigh effort, and a mutation probe after the build commit, because this library carries the central provenance rule.
Rulings after rounds 1 and 2 (2026-10-19):
- The evaluation record is a separate judge input in its own format, which the result producer does not write. Producing it from instrumented evaluator calls is dc-qguw, which blocks infra-m1.3.
- Round 2 closed with no blocking finding. The orchestrator added the four legacy items that were not carried to migration/ports/infra-m1.1.json's not_ported list: OpenFailed, SheetUnmatched, EngineReadFailed and Degraded provenance.
- Follow-ups:

  - dc-u9ss: one shared JSON reader.
  - Notes on infra-m1.2 (CaptureRecord version 2 carries the revision, context fingerprint and shared ranges, and judge checks results.run against them), dc-qguw (the evaluated value or its hash), infra-m7.4 (array anchors, participants, volatile exclusion) and cfml-m1.3 (the evaluation hook).
